title: Stochastic Modelling for Systems Biology
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive introduction to stochastic modelling in systems biology, emphasizing the necessity of probabilistic approaches for accurately capturing the inherent randomness of biological processes. It systematically covers the representation of biochemical networks, foundational probability models, and simulation techniques including Monte Carlo methods and Markov processes. The work explores stochastic chemical kinetics with detailed discussion of the Gillespie algorithm, stochastic Petri nets, and advanced simulation strategies for both well-mixed and spatially extended systems. Case studies illustrate the application of these methods to key biological phenomena such as enzyme kinetics and genetic regulation. The paper further addresses Bayesian inference and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods for parameter estimation and model comparison in stochastic kinetic models, highlighting both exact and approximate computational techniques. Supplementary materials include software tools and SBML models to facilitate practical implementation. This resource serves as a foundational guide for researchers seeking to model, simulate, and infer the dynamics of complex biological systems under uncertainty.

title: Structural biology of HIV.
abstract: The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) genome encodes a total of three structural proteins, two envelope proteins, three enzymes, and six accessory proteins. Studies over the past ten years have provided high-resolution three-dimensional structural information for all of the viral enzymes, structural proteins and envelope proteins, as well as for three of the accessory proteins. In some cases it has been possible to solve the structures of the intact, native proteins, but in most cases structural data were obtained for isolated protein domains, peptidic fragments, or mutants. Peptide complexes with two regulatory RNA fragments and a protein complex with an RNA recognition/encapsidation element have also been structurally characterized. This article summarizes the high-resolution structural information that is currently available for HIV proteins and reviews current structure-function and structure-biological relationships.

title: Structural biology of HIV.
abstract: This study investigates the structural organization and growth dynamics of dense Neisseria gonorrhoeae colonies, focusing on the role of type 4 pilus (T4P) activity and the emergence of spatial heterogeneity. Advanced image analysis and particle tracking methods were developed to resolve single-cell positions within spherical colonies, enabling calculation of radial distribution functions that revealed liquid-like short-range order. Manipulation of T4P retraction phenotypes demonstrated that active T4P force generation accelerates local ordering and density increase but is not essential for local order formation. Over time, all strains exhibited increased density and structural defects independent of T4P activity. Growth dynamics were characterized using both velocity field analysis and lineage tracking, revealing that growth rates are minimal at colony centers and increase toward the periphery. Heterogeneous growth profiles emerged rapidly, persisting even under improved nutrient supply, suggesting mechanical constraints as a contributing factor. Lack of stringent response further accelerated the development of growth heterogeneity, implicating its importance in biofilm maturation. Azithromycin treatment led to rapid, colony-wide growth inhibition, indicating efficient drug penetration. The methodologies established here provide a framework for dissecting the mechanisms underlying spatial heterogeneity and antibiotic response in bacterial biofilms.

title: Synthetic biology - putting engineering into biology
abstract: Synthetic biology is interpreted as the engineering-driven building of increasingly complex biological entities for novel applications. Encouraged by progress in the design of artificial gene networks, de novo DNA synthesis and protein engineering, we review the case for this emerging discipline. Key aspects of an engineering approach are purpose-orientation, deep insight into the underlying scientific principles, a hierarchy of abstraction including suitable interfaces between and within the levels of the hierarchy, standardization and the separation of design and fabrication. Synthetic biology investigates possibilities to implement these requirements into the process of engineering biological systems. This is illustrated on the DNA level by the implementation of engineering-inspired artificial operations such as toggle switching, oscillating or production of spatial patterns. On the protein level, the functionally self-contained domain structure of a number of proteins suggests possibilities for essentially Lego-like recombination which can be exploited for reprogramming DNA binding domain specificities or signaling pathways. Alternatively, computational design emerges to rationally reprogram enzyme function. Finally, the increasing facility of de novo DNA synthesis-synthetic biology's system fabrication process-supplies the possibility to implement novel designs for ever more complex systems. Some of these elements have merged to realize the first tangible synthetic biology applications in the area of manufacturing of pharmaceutical compounds.

title: Synthetic biology - putting engineering into biology
abstract: Synthetic biology represents the application of engineering principles to biological systems, aiming to systematically design and construct novel or improved biological entities for diverse applications. This review explores how foundational engineering concepts—such as modularity, abstraction hierarchies, standardization, and the separation of design from fabrication—are being integrated into biology. Advances in artificial gene networks, de novo DNA synthesis, and protein engineering have enabled the creation of engineered biological functions at multiple levels, including genetic circuits, protein domains, and metabolic pathways. The paper highlights key achievements such as toggle switches, oscillators, spatial pattern formation, and rational enzyme redesign, demonstrating the potential for modular recombination and computational design in synthetic biology. The increasing accessibility of DNA synthesis technologies further supports the realization of complex synthetic systems. While challenges remain due to biological complexity and evolutionary dynamics, the adoption of engineering frameworks is driving progress toward predictable and scalable bioengineering. The review concludes by discussing the implications for bioinformatics and emphasizing the need for continued development of standards and tools to support the systematic engineering of living systems.

title: Synthetic biology: applications come of age
abstract: Synthetic biology is bringing together engineers and biologists to design and build novel biomolecular components, networks and pathways, and to use these constructs to rewire and reprogram organisms. These re-engineered organisms will change our lives over the coming years, leading to cheaper drugs, 'green' means to fuel our cars and targeted therapies for attacking 'superbugs' and diseases, such as cancer. The de novo engineering of genetic circuits, biological modules and synthetic pathways is beginning to address these crucial problems and is being used in related practical applications.

title: Synthetic biology: applications come of age
abstract: Synthetic biology has rapidly evolved from its conceptual origins, inspired by the analogy between biological and electronic circuits, to a robust engineering discipline capable of designing and constructing novel biomolecular components, genetic circuits, and synthetic pathways. Early successes in building synthetic gene networks such as toggle switches and oscillators demonstrated the feasibility of rationally engineering cellular behavior using modular, model-driven approaches. Over the past decade, advances in genomic tools and genetic engineering have enabled the development of increasingly sophisticated biological devices, including memory elements, pulse generators, logic gates, filters, and communication modules. These engineered systems are now transitioning from proof-of-concept demonstrations to practical applications addressing complex societal challenges. This review highlights the emerging real-world impact of synthetic biology in biosensing, therapeutics, biofuel production, pharmaceuticals, and novel biomaterials. The versatility of synthetic biology platforms lies in their ability to integrate sensing and response modules at multiple regulatory levels, enabling precise control over cellular functions. As synthetic biology matures, its multivalent applicability promises transformative solutions across diverse fields, marking a coming-of-age for the discipline.

title: Synthetic DNA Synthesis and Assembly: Putting the Synthetic in Synthetic Biology.
abstract: The chemical synthesis of DNA oligonucleotides and their assembly into synthons, genes, circuits, and even entire genomes by gene synthesis methods has become an enabling technology for modern molecular biology and enables the design, build, test, learn, and repeat cycle underpinning innovations in synthetic biology. In this perspective, we briefly review the techniques and technologies that enable the synthesis of DNA oligonucleotides and their assembly into larger DNA constructs with a focus on recent advancements that have sought to reduce synthesis cost and increase sequence fidelity. The development of lower-cost methods to produce high-quality synthetic DNA will allow for the exploration of larger biological hypotheses by lowering the cost of use and help to close the DNA read-write cost gap.
venue: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology

title: Synthetic DNA Synthesis and Assembly: Putting the Synthetic in Synthetic Biology.
abstract: The rapid advancement of synthetic DNA synthesis and assembly technologies has fundamentally transformed the field of synthetic biology, enabling the rational design and construction of genes, circuits, and entire genomes. This paper provides a concise overview of the key methods underpinning the chemical synthesis of DNA oligonucleotides and their assembly into larger constructs, with particular emphasis on recent innovations aimed at reducing costs and improving sequence fidelity. The integration of next-generation sequencing with high-throughput DNA synthesis has expanded our capacity to read and write genetic information, driving a new era of biological engineering characterized by iterative design, build, test, and learn cycles. Despite significant progress in sequencing technologies, the cost and efficiency of DNA synthesis remain limiting factors; however, emerging approaches are closing this gap, facilitating broader exploration of biological design space. Lower-cost, high-fidelity synthetic DNA production is poised to accelerate research in areas ranging from metabolic engineering to therapeutic development by enabling larger-scale experimentation and more systematic refinement of engineered biological systems.
venue: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology

title: Systems-biology dissection of eukaryotic cell growth
abstract: A recent article in BMC Biology illustrates the use of a systems-biology approach to integrate data across the transcriptome, proteome and metabolome of budding yeast in order to dissect the relationship between nutrient conditions and cell growth.See research article http://jbiol.com/content/6/2/4 and http://www.biomedcentral.com/1741-7007/8/68

title: Systems-biology dissection of eukaryotic cell growth
abstract: Understanding how eukaryotic cell growth is regulated by both genetic and environmental factors remains a central challenge in biology. While recent research has largely focused on genotype-phenotype relationships, the systems-level dissection of environment-phenotype interactions is less explored. This paper reviews advances in systems-biology approaches that integrate transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data to elucidate how nutrient availability influences cell growth in yeast. Using controlled chemostat cultures with defined nutrient limitations and growth rates, recent studies have disentangled the effects of specific nutrients from those of growth rate, revealing both common and nutrient-specific cellular responses. Multivariate analyses demonstrate that carbon limitation elicits the most pronounced transcriptional changes, while growth-rate-dependent responses are robust and largely consistent across different nutrient conditions. Integration of multi-omics data highlights pervasive post-transcriptional regulation and suggests that metabolite levels are buffered by systems-level properties rather than direct enzyme abundance. Although current proteomic and metabolomic coverage is limited compared to transcriptomics, these integrative approaches provide new insights into the molecular pathways linking environmental cues to cell growth and underscore the need for further technological advances to achieve a comprehensive systems-level understanding.

title: Systems biology and genomics of breast cancer.
abstract: It is now accepted that breast cancer is not a single disease, but instead it is composed of a spectrum of tumor subtypes with distinct cellular origins, somatic changes, and etiologies. Gene expression profiling using DNA microarrays has contributed significantly to our understanding of the molecular heterogeneity of breast tumor formation, progression, and recurrence. For example, at least two clinical diagnostic assays exist (i.e., OncotypeDX RS and Mammaprint®) that are able to predict outcome in patients using patterns of gene expression and predetermined mathematical algorithms. In addition, a new molecular taxonomy based upon the inherent, or 'intrinsic,' biology of breast tumors has been developed; this taxonomy is called the 'intrinsic subtypes of breast cancer,' which now identifies five distinct tumor types and a normal breast-like group. Importantly, the intrinsic subtypes of breast cancer predict patient relapse, overall survival, and response to endocrine and chemotherapy regimens. Thus, most of the clinical behavior of a breast tumor is already written in its subtype profile. Here, we describe the discovery and basic biology of the intrinsic subtypes of breast cancer, and detail how this interacts with underlying genetic alternations, response to therapy, and the metastatic process.
venue: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology

title: Systems biology and genomics of breast cancer.
abstract: Breast cancer is now recognized as a heterogeneous disease comprising multiple subtypes with distinct molecular and clinical characteristics. Systems biology approaches, particularly gene expression profiling using DNA microarrays, have enabled the identification of intrinsic breast cancer subtypes—luminal A, luminal B, HER2-enriched, basal-like, and normal breast-like—which are conserved across populations and stages of disease. These subtypes, defined by unique gene expression signatures and validated across numerous independent datasets, correlate strongly with hormone receptor status, genetic alterations, prognosis, and response to therapy. The development of robust classification tools such as the Single Sample Predictor and the PAM50 gene set has facilitated reproducible subtype assignment in clinical samples, including formalin-fixed tissues. Understanding the biology underlying each subtype has revealed key differences in tumor behavior, genetic mutations, and therapeutic vulnerabilities, underscoring the importance of molecular taxonomy in guiding personalized breast cancer management and advancing research into tumor progression and metastasis.
venue: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology

title: Systems biology of the structural proteome
abstract: Background: The success of genome-scale models (GEMs) can be attributed to the high-quality, bottom-up reconstructions of metabolic, protein synthesis, and transcriptional regulatory networks on an organism-specific basis. Such reconstructions are biochemically, genetically, and genomically structured knowledge bases that can be converted into a mathematical format to enable a myriad of computational biological studies. In recent years, genome-scale reconstructions have been extended to include protein structural information, which has opened up new vistas in systems biology research and empowered applications in structural systems biology and systems pharmacology.ResultsHere, we present the generation, application, and dissemination of genome-scale models with protein structures (GEM-PRO) for Escherichia coli and Thermotoga maritima. We show the utility of integrating molecular scale analyses with systems biology approaches by discussing several comparative analyses on the temperature dependence of growth, the distribution of protein fold families, substrate specificity, and characteristic features of whole cell proteomes. Finally, to aid in the grand challenge of big data to knowledge, we provide several explicit tutorials of how protein-related information can be linked to genome-scale models in a public GitHub repository (https://github.com/SBRG/GEMPro/tree/master/GEMPro_recon/). Conclusions: Translating genome-scale, protein-related information to structured data in the format of a GEM provides a direct mapping of gene to gene-product to protein structure to biochemical reaction to network states to phenotypic function. Integration of molecular-level details of individual proteins, such as their physical, chemical, and structural properties, further expands the description of biochemical network-level properties, and can ultimately influence how to model and predict whole cell phenotypes as well as perform comparative systems biology approaches to study differences between organisms. GEM-PRO offers insight into the physical embodiment of an organism’s genotype, and its use in this comparative framework enables exploration of adaptive strategies for these organisms, opening the door to many new lines of research. With these provided tools, tutorials, and background, the reader will be in a position to run GEM-PRO for their own purposes.

title: Systems biology of the structural proteome
abstract: The integration of protein structural data into genome-scale models (GEMs) has advanced systems biology by enabling multi-scale analyses that connect genotype to phenotype through detailed molecular mechanisms. This study presents the development and application of GEMs with protein structures (GEM-PRO) for Escherichia coli and Thermotoga maritima, utilizing a systematic pipeline to map genes to high-quality experimental and homology-modeled protein structures. Comparative analyses demonstrate the utility of GEM-PRO in exploring temperature-dependent growth, protein fold family distributions, substrate specificity, and proteome characteristics. The expanded structural coverage enhances the predictive power of systems biology models, facilitating insights into metabolic specificity, protein complex stoichiometry, and adaptive strategies across organisms. To support dissemination and training, the GEM-PRO knowledgebase and tutorials are made publicly available, empowering researchers to apply this framework to their own studies. Overall, GEM-PRO bridges molecular and systems-level data, providing a comprehensive platform for investigating the structural basis of cellular functions and enabling new directions in comparative and structural systems biology.

title: Ten quick tips for machine learning in computational biology
abstract: Machine learning has become a pivotal tool for many projects in computational biology, bioinformatics, and health informatics. Nevertheless, beginners and biomedical researchers often do not have enough experience to run a data mining project effectively, and therefore can follow incorrect practices, that may lead to common mistakes or over-optimistic results. With this review, we present ten quick tips to take advantage of machine learning in any computational biology context, by avoiding some common errors that we observed hundreds of times in multiple bioinformatics projects. We believe our ten suggestions can strongly help any machine learning practitioner to carry on a successful project in computational biology and related sciences.

title: Ten quick tips for machine learning in computational biology
abstract: Machine learning has become an essential methodology in computational biology, yet many researchers in the life sciences lack the experience to apply it effectively, often resulting in common errors and over-optimistic outcomes. This review presents ten concise tips designed to guide beginners and practitioners in successfully integrating machine learning into computational biology projects. The tips cover critical stages of a project, including proper dataset preparation and arrangement, appropriate splitting of data subsets, clear problem framing, informed algorithm selection, and strategies for handling imbalanced datasets. Additional recommendations address hyper-parameter optimization, overfitting prevention, robust performance evaluation, the use of open-source platforms, and seeking expert feedback. By following these best practices, researchers can avoid frequent pitfalls and enhance the reliability and impact of their machine learning analyses in computational biology and related fields.

title: The biology and function of exosomes in cancer.
abstract: Humans circulate quadrillions of exosomes at all times. Exosomes are a class of extracellular vesicles released by all cells, with a size range of 40-150 nm and a lipid bilayer membrane. Exosomes contain DNA, RNA, and proteins. Exosomes likely remove excess and/or unnecessary constituents from the cells, functioning like garbage bags, although their precise physiological role remains unknown. Additionally, exosomes may mediate specific cell-to-cell communication and activate signaling pathways in cells they fuse or interact with. Exosomes are detected in the tumor microenvironment, and emerging evidence suggests that they play a role in facilitating tumorigenesis by regulating angiogenesis, immunity, and metastasis. Circulating exosomes can be used as liquid biopsies and noninvasive biomarkers for early detection, diagnosis, and treatment of cancer patients.

title: The biology and function of exosomes in cancer.
abstract: Exosomes are small extracellular vesicles of endosomal origin released by all cell types, characterized by their lipid bilayer and diverse molecular cargo including proteins, RNA, and DNA. Their biogenesis involves complex endosomal sorting mechanisms, and their contents reflect the physiological or pathological state of the originating cell. While initially thought to function primarily as cellular waste disposal units, exosomes are now recognized as dynamic mediators of intercellular communication, capable of transferring bioactive molecules to recipient cells and modulating signaling pathways. In cancer, exosome production is elevated and their heterogeneity is enhanced, contributing to tumor progression by influencing angiogenesis, immune responses, and metastasis. The molecular composition of cancer-derived exosomes offers potential for noninvasive diagnostics and liquid biopsy approaches, although challenges remain in distinguishing exosomes from other extracellular vesicles and elucidating the specificity of their cargo selection. Overall, exosomes play multifaceted roles in cancer biology and represent promising targets for biomarker discovery and therapeutic intervention.

title: The biology of extracellular vesicles: The known unknowns
abstract: For many years, double-layer phospholipid membrane vesicles, released by most cells, were not considered to be of biological significance. This stance has dramatically changed with the recognition of extracellular vesicles (EVs) as carriers of biologically active molecules that can traffic to local or distant targets and execute defined biological functions. The dimensionality of the field has expanded with the appreciation of diverse types of EVs and the complexity of vesicle biogenesis, cargo loading, release pathways, targeting mechanisms, and vesicle processing. With the expanded interest in the field and the accelerated rate of publications on EV structure and function in diverse biomedical fields, it has become difficult to distinguish between well-established biological features of EV and the untested hypotheses or speculative assumptions that await experimental proof. With the growing interest despite the limited evidence, we sought in this essay to formulate a set of unsolved mysteries in the field, sort out established data from fascinating hypotheses, and formulate several challenging questions that must be answered for the field to advance.

title: The biology of extracellular vesicles: The known unknowns
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-bound particles released by cells that play crucial roles in intercellular communication, physiological regulation, and disease processes. Despite significant advances in characterizing their biogenesis, cargo, and functional diversity, many aspects of EV biology remain incompletely understood. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the molecular mechanisms governing EV formation, release, and uptake, highlighting the heterogeneity of vesicle subtypes such as exosomes and microvesicles. It discusses the challenges in distinguishing EV populations, standardizing isolation techniques, and interpreting functional assays due to overlapping markers and methodological limitations. The paper also explores emerging evidence for EV involvement in immune modulation, cancer progression, and tissue regeneration while emphasizing unresolved questions regarding their in vivo dynamics, specificity of cargo selection, and physiological relevance. By outlining these “known unknowns,” the review underscores the need for rigorous experimental approaches and novel technologies to unravel the complexities of EV biology and harness their potential as diagnostic and therapeutic tools.

title: The DAVID Gene Functional Classification Tool: a novel biological module-centric algorithm to functionally analyze large gene lists
abstract: The DAVID Gene Functional Classification Tool http://david.abcc.ncifcrf.gov uses a novel agglomeration algorithm to condense a list of genes or associated biological terms into organized classes of related genes or biology, called biological modules. This organization is accomplished by mining the complex biological co-occurrences found in multiple sources of functional annotation. It is a powerful method to group functionally related genes and terms into a manageable number of biological modules for efficient interpretation of gene lists in a network context.

title: The DAVID Gene Functional Classification Tool: a novel biological module-centric algorithm to functionally analyze large gene lists
abstract: The DAVID Gene Functional Classification Tool introduces a novel module-centric algorithm that organizes large gene lists into biologically meaningful groups by leveraging a fuzzy agglomeration approach based on global annotation profile similarity. Unlike traditional methods that rely on sequence homology or predefined categories, DAVID measures functional relationships between genes by analyzing the overlap of diverse annotation terms from multiple databases, enabling the identification of broader and more functionally relevant gene modules. The tool’s fuzzy clustering allows genes and terms to participate in multiple modules, reflecting the complex many-to-many relationships inherent in biological systems. This approach reduces redundancy, enhances interpretability, and facilitates visualization of gene-term networks, providing researchers with an efficient means to extract biological insights from high-throughput genomic or proteomic data. The paper details the underlying algorithms, demonstrates key functionalities, and highlights how DAVID enables rapid and comprehensive functional analysis of large-scale gene lists.

title: The Evolutionary synthesis : perspectives on the unification of biology
abstract: It is common knowledge that the theories proposed by Darwin in his Origin encountered massive resistance. But there were considerable differences in the degree of acceptance of his various theories, particularly among the biological disciplines. The naturalists (taxonomists), for instance, favored evolutionary theories different from those of the experimental zoologists. The paleontologists, again, had preferences somewhat different from those of the students of living organisms. The result was one controversy after another, until finally, in the years 1937 to 1947, a general consensus was reached, now referred to as the evolutionary synthesis. In order to understand why such a synthesis was necessary and how it was accomplished, one must review the entire history of the Darwinian controversies after 1859. Within this period a number of shorter periods can be distinguised, each of which became the background for the ensuing period.

title: The Evolutionary synthesis : perspectives on the unification of biology
abstract: This paper examines the role of active information in evolutionary search algorithms by analyzing the Avida digital organism platform, which evolves logic functions using only nand gates. Drawing on conservation of information and no free lunch theorems, we demonstrate that successful search performance in Avida depends critically on domain-specific prior knowledge, such as reward stair steps that guide the synthesis of increasingly complex logic functions. Empirical evaluation reveals that removing these sources of active information significantly impairs search efficiency, while eliminating deleterious instructions enhances it. We further show that alternative evolutionary strategies leveraging the same prior knowledge can outperform Avida in generating target logic functions with fewer instructions. These findings highlight the necessity of external information for effective search in complex spaces and provide a quantitative framework for measuring the contribution of such information to algorithmic performance in digital evolution systems.

title: The expanded biology of serotonin.
abstract: Serotonin is perhaps best known as a neurotransmitter that modulates neural activity and a wide range of neuropsychological processes, and drugs that target serotonin receptors are used widely in psychiatry and neurology. However, most serotonin is found outside the central nervous system, and virtually all of the 15 serotonin receptors are expressed outside as well as within the brain. Serotonin regulates numerous biological processes including cardiovascular function, bowel motility, ejaculatory latency, and bladder control. Additionally, new work suggests that serotonin may regulate some processes, including platelet aggregation, by receptor-independent, transglutaminase-dependent covalent linkage to cellular proteins. We review this new 'expanded serotonin biology' and discuss how drugs targeting specific serotonin receptors are beginning to help treat a wide range of diseases.

title: The expanded biology of serotonin.
abstract: Serotonin, traditionally recognized as a central nervous system neurotransmitter influencing mood and behavior, is now understood to have far broader biological roles. Most serotonin resides outside the brain, and its diverse receptor subtypes are widely expressed throughout the body. Recent advances reveal that serotonin regulates a variety of physiological processes, including cardiovascular function, gastrointestinal motility, platelet aggregation, and genitourinary control. Notably, serotonin can act through both receptor-mediated mechanisms and receptor-independent covalent modifications of cellular proteins. This expanded understanding of serotonin biology has significant implications for drug development, as therapeutics targeting specific serotonin receptors are increasingly used to treat a wide spectrum of neuropsychiatric and medical disorders. The complex interplay between serotonin signaling in multiple organ systems underscores the need for careful consideration of systemic effects when designing serotonergic drugs, with the potential to improve therapeutic efficacy and minimize adverse outcomes.

title: The human keratins: biology and pathology
abstract: The keratins are the typical intermediate filament proteins of epithelia, showing an outstanding degree of molecular diversity. Heteropolymeric filaments are formed by pairing of type I and type II molecules. In humans 54 functional keratin genes exist. They are expressed in highly specific patterns related to the epithelial type and stage of cellular differentiation. About half of all keratins—including numerous keratins characterized only recently—are restricted to the various compartments of hair follicles. As part of the epithelial cytoskeleton, keratins are important for the mechanical stability and integrity of epithelial cells and tissues. Moreover, some keratins also have regulatory functions and are involved in intracellular signaling pathways, e.g. protection from stress, wound healing, and apoptosis. Applying the new consensus nomenclature, this article summarizes, for all human keratins, their cell type and tissue distribution and their functional significance in relation to transgenic mouse models and human hereditary keratin diseases. Furthermore, since keratins also exhibit characteristic expression patterns in human tumors, several of them (notably K5, K7, K8/K18, K19, and K20) have great importance in immunohistochemical tumor diagnosis of carcinomas, in particular of unclear metastases and in precise classification and subtyping. Future research might open further fields of clinical application for this remarkable protein family.

title: The human keratins: biology and pathology
abstract: Keratins are a diverse family of intermediate filament proteins fundamental to the structure and function of epithelial cells. In humans, 54 functional keratin genes exhibit highly specific expression patterns according to epithelial type and differentiation stage, with approximately half restricted to hair follicle compartments. Keratins form heteropolymeric filaments through obligate pairing of type I and type II molecules, providing mechanical stability and integrity to epithelial tissues via interactions with cell junctions such as desmosomes. Beyond their structural role, certain keratins participate in regulatory processes including stress response, wound healing, and apoptosis. Advances in molecular characterization and the adoption of a consensus nomenclature have clarified the distribution, structure, and function of all human keratins, facilitating insights from transgenic mouse models and the study of hereditary keratin disorders. Additionally, distinct keratin expression profiles serve as valuable immunohistochemical markers in tumor diagnosis and subtyping, particularly for carcinomas with unclear metastases. Ongoing research continues to expand the clinical relevance of this protein family in both diagnostic and therapeutic contexts.

title: The molecular biology of apoptosis.
abstract: All multicellular organisms have mechanisms for killing their own cells, and use physiological cell death for defence, development, homeostasis, and aging. Apoptosis is a morphologically recognizable form of cell death that is implemented by a mechanism that has been conserved throughout evolution from nematode to man. Thus homologs of the genes that implement cell death in nematodes also do so in mammals, but in mammals the process is considerably more complex, involving multiple isoforms of the components of the cell death machinery. In some circumstances this allows independent regulation of pathways that converge upon a common end point. A molecular understanding of this mechanism may allow design of therapies that either enhance or block cell death at will.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: The molecular biology of apoptosis.
abstract: Apoptosis, a genetically programmed form of cell death, is essential for development, homeostasis, defense, and aging in multicellular organisms. This review explores the molecular mechanisms underlying apoptosis, highlighting its evolutionary conservation from nematodes to mammals. Key regulatory genes and proteins, such as the cysteine protease Ced-3 in Caenorhabditis elegans and its mammalian homologs (including ICE and CPP32), are discussed in relation to their roles in initiating and executing cell death via proteolytic cascades. The process of apoptosis is divided into distinct phases: initiation by internal or external stimuli, signal transduction, effector activation involving proteases, and postmortem events such as DNA fragmentation and cell clearance. The interplay between pro-apoptotic and anti-apoptotic factors, notably the Bcl-2 family, allows for fine regulation of cell death pathways. Understanding these molecular events provides insight into the physiological roles of apoptosis and suggests potential therapeutic strategies for diseases involving aberrant cell survival or death.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: The Weak Hydrogen Bond: In Structural Chemistry and Biology
abstract: The weak hydrogen bond, also known as non-conventional hydrogen bond, has been the subject of intense scrutiny over recent years in several fields, in particular structural chemistry, structural biology, and the pharmaceutical sciences. Today, there is a large body of experimental and theoretical evidence confirming that hydrogen bonds like C-H···O, N-H···π, C-H···π and even bonds like O-H··· metal play distinctive roles in molecular recognition, guiding molecular association, and in determining molecular and supramolecular architectures. The relevant compound classes include organometallic complexes, organic and bio-organic systems, as well as DNA and proteins.

title: The Weak Hydrogen Bond: In Structural Chemistry and Biology
abstract: This work provides a comprehensive examination of the weak hydrogen bond, exploring its significance and diverse roles in structural chemistry and biology. Drawing on extensive crystallographic evidence, the authors analyze the nature, energetics, and geometrical preferences of weak hydrogen bonds, distinguishing them from classical strong hydrogen bonds. The book discusses the impact of these interactions on molecular recognition, crystal engineering, and biological macromolecular structures, highlighting their importance in stabilizing protein and nucleic acid conformations as well as influencing molecular assembly in solid-state materials. By integrating theoretical insights with experimental data, this volume advances the understanding of weak hydrogen bonding as a fundamental force shaping chemical and biological systems.

title: Universally Sloppy Parameter Sensitivities in Systems Biology Models
abstract: Quantitative computational models play an increasingly important role in modern biology. Such models typically involve many free parameters, and assigning their values is often a substantial obstacle to model development. Directly measuring in vivo biochemical parameters is difficult, and collectively fitting them to other experimental data often yields large parameter uncertainties. Nevertheless, in earlier work we showed in a growth-factor-signaling model that collective fitting could yield well-constrained predictions, even when it left individual parameters very poorly constrained. We also showed that the model had a “sloppy” spectrum of parameter sensitivities, with eigenvalues roughly evenly distributed over many decades. Here we use a collection of models from the literature to test whether such sloppy spectra are common in systems biology. Strikingly, we find that every model we examine has a sloppy spectrum of sensitivities. We also test several consequences of this sloppiness for building predictive models. In particular, sloppiness suggests that collective fits to even large amounts of ideal time-series data will often leave many parameters poorly constrained. Tests over our model collection are consistent with this suggestion. This difficulty with collective fits may seem to argue for direct parameter measurements, but sloppiness also implies that such measurements must be formidably precise and complete to usefully constrain many model predictions. We confirm this implication in our growth-factor-signaling model. Our results suggest that sloppy sensitivity spectra are universal in systems biology models. The prevalence of sloppiness highlights the power of collective fits and suggests that modelers should focus on predictions rather than on parameters.

title: Universally Sloppy Parameter Sensitivities in Systems Biology Models
abstract: Quantitative models in systems biology often involve numerous parameters whose precise values are difficult to determine, posing a challenge for model development and predictive accuracy. Previous studies have shown that even when individual parameter values are poorly constrained, collective fitting to experimental data can still yield reliable model predictions, a phenomenon attributed to “sloppy” parameter sensitivities—where model behavior is highly sensitive to only a few specific parameter combinations. In this study, we systematically analyze 17 published systems biology models and find that all exhibit sloppy spectra of parameter sensitivities, suggesting that sloppiness is a universal feature of such models. We demonstrate that, due to this sloppiness, collective fitting to extensive time-series data typically leaves many parameters poorly constrained, while direct parameter measurements would need to be exceptionally precise and comprehensive to significantly improve predictive power. These findings highlight the limitations of focusing on individual parameter estimation and suggest that modelers should prioritize predictive accuracy over parameter precision when developing and validating systems biology models.

title: Vibrations, quanta and biology
abstract: Abstract Quantum biology is an emerging field of research that concerns itself with the experimental and theoretical exploration of non-trivial quantum phenomena in biological systems. In this tutorial overview we aim to bring out fundamental assumptions and questions in the field, identify basic design principles and develop a key underlying theme – the dynamics of quantum dynamical networks in the presence of an environment and the fruitful interplay that the two may enter. At the hand of three biological phenomena whose understanding is held to require quantum mechanical processes, namely excitation and charge transfer in photosynthetic complexes, magneto-reception in birds and the olfactory sense, we demonstrate that this underlying theme encompasses them all, thus suggesting its wider relevance as an archetypical framework for quantum biology.

title: Vibrations, quanta and biology
abstract: Quantum biology explores the presence and functional significance of non-trivial quantum phenomena in biological systems, challenging the traditional view that warm, noisy environments preclude quantum effects. This tutorial overview examines the fundamental assumptions and open questions in the field, emphasizing the central role of quantum dynamical networks interacting with complex environments. By analyzing three key biological processes—excitation and charge transfer in photosynthetic complexes, avian magnetoreception, and olfaction—the paper demonstrates that a constructive interplay between quantum dynamics and environmental fluctuations can enhance biological function. The discussion highlights how evolutionary adaptation may exploit such quantum effects for improved efficiency and novel functionalities, suggesting generalizable design principles for both understanding biology and developing bio-inspired technologies. The review underscores the importance of refined experimental techniques and advanced theoretical models to unravel these mechanisms, positioning the interplay of vibrations, quanta, and environment as a unifying framework for future research in quantum biology.

title: What is Systems Biology?
abstract: Systems biology is increasingly popular, but to many biologists it remains unclear what this new discipline actually encompasses. This brief personal perspective starts by outlining the asthetic qualities that motivate systems biologists, discusses which activities do not belong to the core of systems biology, and finally explores the crucial link with synthetic biology. It concludes by attempting to define systems biology as the research endeavor that aims at providing the scientific foundation for successful synthetic biology.

title: What is Systems Biology?
abstract: This perspective article addresses the ongoing ambiguity surrounding the definition of systems biology, a field characterized by its interdisciplinary nature and rapid growth. The author explores the aesthetic motivations that drive systems biologists, emphasizing the interplay of diversity, simplicity, and complexity as central qualities that distinguish the discipline. By examining what systems biology is not, the article clarifies its boundaries and distinguishes it from related research activities. The discussion highlights the importance of computational modeling and integrative analysis of large-scale biological data, while also underscoring the field’s foundational role in enabling synthetic biology. Ultimately, the article proposes that systems biology should be defined as the scientific endeavor aimed at providing a comprehensive framework for understanding and engineering biological systems, thus laying the groundwork for advances in synthetic biology.

title: WikiPathways: Pathway Editing for the People
abstract: WikiPathways provides a collaborative platform for creating, updating, and sharing pathway diagrams and serves as an example of content curation by the biology community.

title: WikiPathways: Pathway Editing for the People
abstract: The rapid expansion of biological data presents significant challenges for the curation and integration of pathway information, which is essential for understanding complex biological systems. Traditional pathway databases rely on small, specialized teams and static representations, limiting community participation and the ability to keep pace with new discoveries. WikiPathways addresses these limitations by providing an open, collaborative platform that enables the broader scientific community to contribute, edit, and maintain biological pathways using a user-friendly web interface and an embedded graphical editing tool. By leveraging the familiar wiki model and integrating pathway-specific features such as direct annotation with public databases and literature references, WikiPathways lowers barriers to participation and facilitates continuous updating and peer review. This community-driven approach enhances the accessibility, accuracy, and relevance of pathway information, offering a scalable solution to the challenges posed by the ongoing growth of biological data.

title: Wnt signaling in cancer.
abstract: Aberrant regulation of the Wnt signaling pathway is a prevalent theme in cancer biology. From the earliest observation that Wnt overexpression could lead to malignant transformation of mouse mammary tissue to the most recent genetic discoveries gleaned from tumor genome sequencing, the Wnt pathway continues to evolve as a central mechanism in cancer biology. This article summarizes the evidence supporting a role for Wnt signaling in human cancer. This includes a review of the genetic mutations affecting Wnt pathway components, as well as some of epigenetic mechanisms that alter expression of genes relevant to Wnt. I also highlight some research on the cooperativity of Wnt with other signaling pathways in cancer. Finally, some emphasis is placed on laboratory research that provides a proof of concept for the therapeutic inhibition of Wnt signaling in cancer.
venue: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology

title: Wnt signaling in cancer.
abstract: Aberrant Wnt signaling is a hallmark of many human cancers, with both genetic and epigenetic alterations contributing to tumorigenesis. This review outlines the historical and molecular basis for the role of Wnt pathway dysregulation in cancer, highlighting key discoveries such as the involvement of APC, β-catenin, Axin, and WTX in tumor suppression and oncogenesis. Mutations that activate β-catenin or inactivate components of its destruction complex are prevalent in colorectal, hepatocellular, and other cancers. Additionally, epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation and chromatin modifications, frequently silence Wnt antagonists such as sFRP family members, further promoting oncogenic signaling. The interplay between Wnt and other pathways is also discussed, underscoring the complexity of its role in cancer biology. Finally, emerging therapeutic strategies targeting Wnt signaling are considered, providing proof-of-concept for pathway inhibition as a viable approach in cancer treatment.
venue: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology

title: Application of ChatGPT in Business Management and Strategic Decision Making
abstract: In the era of globalisation and the information technology revolution, businesses are faced with increasingly complex and dynamic challenges. Business managers and company executives are required to make the right and fast strategic decisions to maintain the company's competitive advantage in a rapidly changing market. Along with the development of AI and NLP, technology applications in business management have undergone significant developments. One of the latest promising innovations is the use of ChatGPT in the context of business management and strategic decision-making. This research aims to investigate the application of ChatGPT in the context of business management and strategic decision-making. This research is a literature review that adopts a qualitative method approach, which means it will analyse and interpret data by relying on information and text from various sources. The study results show that the application of ChatGPT in business management and strategic decision-making offers great potential for improving the efficiency, productivity and quality of decision-making. With its ability to provide quick responses, in-depth data analysis and personalised interactions, ChatGPT can be a valuable intelligent assistant for enterprises. Key benefits of using ChatGPT in business management are improved customer service, business process automation, and more data-driven decision-making.

title: Application of ChatGPT in Business Management and Strategic Decision Making
abstract: This study explores the integration of ChatGPT, an advanced AI language model, into business management and strategic decision-making processes. Through a qualitative literature review, the research examines how ChatGPT's capabilities in natural language processing and data analysis can enhance managerial efficiency, productivity, and decision quality. The findings indicate that ChatGPT offers significant benefits, including improved customer service through intelligent chatbots, automation of business processes, and support for data-driven strategies. However, the study also highlights challenges such as data security, response reliability, and potential misinterpretation in complex scenarios. Overall, the research concludes that while ChatGPT presents promising opportunities for organizations seeking to optimize operations and strategic outcomes, careful consideration of its limitations is essential for effective implementation in corporate environments.

title: Asian management in the 21st century
abstract: Contrary to popular opinion, the crucial elements of the management process show strong continuity over time, but differ from one country to another, as a function of the local culture. Recent research reveals fundamental differences in the goals of business leaders from different societies. The article explores general characteristics of Asian management as opposed to management elsewhere, and what the study of Asian management and its cultural origins mean for the emerging Asian multinationals and for the state of the art in management research worldwide in the twenty-first century.

title: Asian management in the 21st century
abstract: This paper challenges the prevailing notion that management practices are universally applicable and primarily shaped by contemporary trends, arguing instead that the core elements of management remain stable over time but vary significantly across societies due to cultural differences. Drawing on historical and literary examples from China and Russia, the study illustrates how deeply rooted cultural values influence management approaches and outcomes, with particular attention to the enduring characteristics of Asian management. The analysis highlights that while technological advancements may alter management practices, they do not fundamentally change underlying cultural values. The paper concludes that understanding the cultural origins of Asian management is essential for both emerging Asian multinationals and the advancement of global management research in the twenty-first century.

title: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF NATURAL DISASTERS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT IN TOURISM
abstract: Natural disasters are a critical factor for the development of business management in the tourism industry, leading to an increasing number of publications on the relationship between natural disasters and tourism business management (ND&T). In order to identify the research status of ND&T and explore the direction for future research, this paper collects 335 publications related to ND&T and develops a bibliometric analysis of the existing publications. First, we map the leading countries/regions, institutions, authors, and journals of ND&T to visualize the general analysis. Then the cooperation network is provided to show the collaboration relationship between countries/regions, institutions, and authors. Third, we introduce the keyword analysis to obtain research hotspots of ND&T. And finally, we explore the research theme analysis through literature review and conclude four topics. The findings of the topic analysis suggest that research on ND&T is receiving increasing attention, and more cooperation is required in the future to deepen the theoretical and empirical focus on tourists.
venue: Journal of Business and Economic Management

title: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF NATURAL DISASTERS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT IN TOURISM
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research on the intersection of natural disasters and business management in tourism (ND&T). Drawing on 335 English-language publications from the Web of Science database spanning 1992 to 2020, the analysis maps leading countries, institutions, authors, and journals, and visualizes collaboration networks within the field. Keyword co-occurrence and burst detection methods are employed to identify research hotspots and emerging trends. The literature review synthesizes four main thematic areas: the impact of natural disasters on tourism, disaster prevention strategies, post-disaster revival of tourism, and the reciprocal effects of tourism on natural disasters. Results reveal a growing scholarly focus on ND&T, with increasing publication output and expanding international collaboration. However, findings highlight the need for deeper theoretical development and more empirical research centered on tourists. The study provides a structured overview of the ND&T research landscape and offers guidance for future studies aiming to enhance resilience and management practices in tourism facing natural disasters.
venue: Journal of Business and Economic Management

title: A Critical Look at the Use of SEM in International Business Research
abstract: Purpose – Structural equation modeling (SEM) has been widely used to examine complex research models in international business and marketing research. While the covariance-based SEM (CB-SEM) approach is dominant, the authors argue that the field’s dynamic nature and the sometimes early stage of theory development more often require a partial least squares SEM (PLS-SEM) approach. The purpose of this paper is to critically review the application of SEM techniques in the field. Design/methodology/approach – The authors searched six journals with an international business (and marketing) focus (Management International Review, Journal of International Business Studies, Journal of International Management, International Marketing Review, Journal of World Business, International Business Review) from 1990 to 2013. The authors reviewed all articles that apply SEM, analyzed their research objectives and methodology choices, and assessed whether the PLS-SEM papers followed the best practices outlined in the past. ...

title: A Critical Look at the Use of SEM in International Business Research
abstract: This paper critically examines the application of structural equation modeling (SEM) in international business research, focusing on the relative use and justification of covariance-based SEM (CB-SEM) and partial least squares SEM (PLS-SEM). Through a systematic review of six leading international business and marketing journals from 1990 to 2013, the study finds that CB-SEM overwhelmingly dominates, with PLS-SEM underutilized despite its advantages for exploratory and predictive research in dynamic and complex environments. The analysis reveals that researchers often select PLS-SEM primarily due to data or sampling constraints rather than leveraging its methodological strengths for theory development. The paper identifies a lack of adherence to best practices in PLS-SEM application and highlights missed opportunities for advancing theory building in the field. By offering practical guidelines and recommendations, this study contributes to improving methodological rigor and encourages more informed choices between SEM approaches to better align with research objectives in international business and marketing.

title: A Critical Success Factors Model for ERP Implementation
abstract: An effective IT infrastructure can support a business vision and strategy; a poor, decentralized one can break a company. More and more companies are turning to off-the-shelf ERP (enterprise resource planning) solutions for IT planning and legacy systems management. The authors have developed a framework to help managers successfully plan and implement an ERP project.

title: A Critical Success Factors Model for ERP Implementation
abstract: This nested qualitative study explores patient and physiotherapist perspectives on Cognitive Muscular TherapyTM (CMT), a novel behavioural intervention for knee osteoarthritis that integrates muscle biofeedback and psychological strategies to target muscle overactivity. Five physiotherapists, trained in a structured CMT protocol, delivered seven individualized sessions to patients with knee osteoarthritis, who also accessed online educational materials. Semi-structured interviews conducted post-intervention revealed a process of belief change among both patients and physiotherapists, organized into three phases: identifying maladaptive pain beliefs, challenging and validating new beliefs through experience, and embedding these changes into self-management practices. Participants described developing a new understanding of their condition, recognizing the interplay between psychological factors and muscle activity, and gaining confidence in managing knee pain. The findings highlight the psychological shifts enabled by CMT and suggest its potential to facilitate reconceptualization of knee osteoarthritis, supporting improved self-management and engagement in daily activities.

title: Blockchains for Business Process Management - Challenges and Opportunities
abstract: Blockchain technology offers a sizable promise to rethink the way interorganizational business processes are managed because of its potential to realize execution without a central party serving as a single point of trust (and failure). To stimulate research on this promise and the limits thereof, in this article, we outline the challenges and opportunities of blockchain for business process management (BPM). We first reflect how blockchains could be used in the context of the established BPM lifecycle and second how they might become relevant beyond. We conclude our discourse with a summary of seven research directions for investigating the application of blockchain technology in the context of BPM.
venue: ACM Transactions on Management Information Systems

title: Blockchains for Business Process Management - Challenges and Opportunities
abstract: Blockchain technology presents significant potential to transform inter-organizational business process management (BPM) by enabling process execution without reliance on a central trusted authority. This paper explores the challenges and opportunities that arise from integrating blockchain into BPM, examining its impact on the established BPM lifecycle and considering its broader implications for core BPM capabilities. The discussion highlights how blockchain’s decentralized consensus mechanisms, tamper-proof recordkeeping, and trustless transaction execution can address longstanding issues in collaborative process design and execution across organizational boundaries. The paper concludes by identifying seven key research directions that will shape future investigations into the effective application of blockchain technology within BPM contexts.
venue: ACM Transactions on Management Information Systems

title: Business intelligence and big data in hospitality and tourism: a systematic literature review
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the extent to which Business Intelligence and Big Data feature within academic research in hospitality and tourism published until 2016, by identifying research gaps and future developments and designing an agenda for future research. Design/methodology/approach The study consists of a systematic quantitative literature review of academic articles indexed on the Scopus and Web of Science databases. The articles were reviewed based on the following features: research topic; conceptual and theoretical characterization; sources of data; type of data and size; data collection methods; data analysis techniques; and data reporting and visualization. Findings Findings indicate an increase in hospitality and tourism management literature applying analytical techniques to large quantities of data. However, this research field is fairly fragmented in scope and limited in methodologies and displays several gaps. A conceptual framework that helps to identify critical business problems and links the domains of business intelligence and big data to tourism and hospitality management and development is missing. Moreover, epistemological dilemmas and consequences for theory development of big data-driven knowledge are still a terra incognita. Last, despite calls for more integration of management and data science, cross-disciplinary collaborations with computer and data scientists are rather episodic and related to specific types of work and research. Research limitations/implications This work is based on academic articles published before 2017; hence, scientific outputs published after the moment of writing have not been included. A rich research agenda is designed. Originality/value This study contributes to explore in depth and systematically to what extent hospitality and tourism scholars are aware of and working intendedly on business intelligence and big data. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, it is the first systematic literature review within hospitality and tourism research dealing with business intelligence and big data.
venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Business intelligence and big data in hospitality and tourism: a systematic literature review
abstract: This paper presents a systematic quantitative literature review of academic research on business intelligence (BI) and big data (BD) in hospitality and tourism published up to 2016. Using articles indexed in Scopus and Web of Science, the review analyzes research topics, conceptual frameworks, data sources and types, collection methods, analytical techniques, and reporting practices. Findings reveal a growing application of analytical methods to large datasets in the field, but also highlight fragmentation in scope, limited methodological diversity, and a lack of integrative conceptual frameworks linking BI and BD to hospitality and tourism management. The review identifies significant epistemological challenges and a scarcity of cross-disciplinary collaboration with data science, suggesting that theoretical development remains nascent. The study concludes with a comprehensive research agenda to address these gaps and advance the integration of BI and BD in hospitality and tourism scholarship. This is the first systematic literature review to comprehensively map the intersection of BI, BD, and hospitality and tourism research.
venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Business Practices in Small Firms in Developing Countries
abstract: Management has a large effect on the productivity of medium and large firms. But does management matter in micro and small firms, where the majority of the labor force in developing countries works? We develop 26 questions that measure business practices in marketing, stock-keeping, record-keeping, and financial planning. These questions have been administered in surveys in Bangladesh, Chile, Ghana, Kenya, Mexico, Nigeria, and Sri Lanka. We show that variation in business practices explains as much of the variation in outcomes-sales, profits, and labor productivity and total factor productivity-in microenterprises as in larger enterprises. Panel data from three countries indicate that better business practices predict higher survival rates and faster sales growth. The association of business practices with firm outcomes is robust to including numerous measures of the owner's human capital. We find that owners with higher human capital, children of entrepreneurs, and firms with employees employ better business practices. Data, as supplemental material, are available at http://dx.doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2016.2492 . This paper was accepted by Toby Stuart, entrepreneurship and innovation.

title: Business Practices in Small Firms in Developing Countries
abstract: This paper investigates the role of business practices in micro and small firms across seven developing countries by introducing a standardized set of 26 survey questions covering marketing, stock-keeping, record-keeping, and financial planning. Analysis reveals that variation in these business practices explains a significant share of differences in firm performance—measured by sales, profits, labor productivity, and total factor productivity—comparable to effects observed in larger firms. Panel data from three countries further show that better business practices predict higher firm survival rates and faster sales growth over time. The relationship between business practices and outcomes remains robust after controlling for owner human capital, with evidence that higher human capital, entrepreneurial family background, and having employees are associated with better practices. Competition shows weaker associations. Auditing exercises confirm the reliability of self-reported data. The findings suggest that improving business practices can substantially enhance performance even among the smallest firms in developing countries, challenging the view that formal management is less relevant in this context.

title: Business process management - at the crossroads
abstract: PurposeBusiness process management (BPM) has attracted much focus throughout the years, yet there have been calls questioning the future of BPM. The purpose of this paper is to explore the current state of the field through a dynamic literature review and identify the main challenges for its future development.Design/methodology/approachA dynamic co-citation network analysis identifies the “evolution” of knowledge of BPM and the most influential works. The results present the developed BPM subthemes in the form of clusters.FindingsThe focus within the field has shifted from facilitating wide-ranging business performance improvements to creating introverted optimizations within a particular BPM subgroup. The BPM field has thus experienced strong fragmentation throughout the years and has accrued into self-fueling subareas of BPM research such as business process modeling and workflow management. Those subareas often neglect related disciplines in other management, process modeling and organizational improvement fields.Research limitations/implicationsThe study is limited by the initial keyword choice of the authors. The subsequent co-citation analysis ameliorates the subjectivity since it produces a data set and contributions based on references.Originality/valueA new combination of historical development and the state-of-the-art of the BPM field, by employing a co-citation and cluster analysis. This dynamic literature review presents the current state of the theoretical core and attempts to identify the crossroads that BPM has reached. The study can be replicated in the future to track the changes in the field.

title: Business process management - at the crossroads
abstract: This paper examines the current state and future direction of business process management (BPM), a field that has evolved from broad performance improvement initiatives to increasingly specialized subdomains such as process modeling and workflow management. Using dynamic co-citation and cluster analysis, the study maps the evolution of BPM knowledge, identifies influential works, and delineates prevailing research themes. Findings reveal significant fragmentation within BPM, with research often isolated from related management and organizational improvement disciplines. The analysis highlights a lack of consensus on core concepts and persistent ambiguity regarding BPM’s identity, which may hinder both academic progress and practical relevance. The study’s methodological approach offers a replicable framework for tracking changes in the field over time and contributes to clarifying the theoretical core of BPM at a critical juncture in its development.

title: Business Process Modeling, Simulation and Design
abstract: Business Process Modeling, Simulation and Design, Third Edition provides students with a comprehensive coverage of a range of analytical tools used to model, analyze, understand, and ultimately design business processes.  The new edition of this very successful textbook includes a wide range of approaches such as graphical flowcharting tools, cycle time and capacity analyses, queuing models, discrete-event simulation, simulation-optimization, and data mining for process analytics.  While most textbooks on business process management either focus on the intricacies of computer simulation or managerial aspects of business processes, this textbook does both. It presents the tools to design business processes and management techniques on operating them efficiently.  The book focuses on the use of discrete event simulation as the main tool for analyzing, modeling, and designing effective business processes. The integration of graphic user-friendly simulation software enables a systematic approach to create optimal designs.

title: Business Process Modeling, Simulation and Design
abstract: This comprehensive text provides an integrated approach to business process modeling, simulation, and design, emphasizing the critical role of process management in organizational performance and strategy. Covering foundational concepts such as process types, architecture, and workflow management systems, the book guides readers through incremental improvement, reengineering, and the implementation of Six Sigma quality programs. It presents a structured framework for business process design projects, supported by practical tools for process flow analysis and workflow optimization. The text delves into managing process flows, including cycle time and capacity analysis, and introduces queuing theory as a basis for understanding system dynamics. Simulation techniques are explored in depth, with practical guidance on model development using ExtendSim and spreadsheet tools, as well as methods for input and output data analysis. Advanced topics include simulation optimization, business process analytics, benchmarking, and the application of data mining and process mining within business process management systems. Through illustrative examples and case studies from diverse industries, the book equips students and practitioners with the methodologies and analytical tools necessary to design, analyze, simulate, and optimize business processes for enhanced efficiency and effectiveness.

title: Economic Empowerment of Small Businesses Through Zakat Funds at the Amil Zakat Infaq Shadaqah Institute in Surakarta
abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the management and economic empowerment of small business communities and the form of empowerment carried out by the two LazisMu. This type of research belongs to the category of field research with a qualitative research approach. Data sources were obtained through observation, interviews, and documentation. Data analysis techniques are reducing data, presenting data, and drawing conclusions. The results of the research include: The collected zakat funds are given to the poor who can do entrepreneurship on the recommendation of the Muhammadiyah Business Leadership or Charity. Management and economic empowerment of small business communities, LazisMu distributes zakat funds directly to individuals and through institutions after an investigation by LazisMu, Zakat funds given can be empowered in various programs that can improve the welfare of the Ummah as currently done by LazisMu is given in the form of business capital. Among them are LazisMu UMS through the By Friend and By Requets programs including business capital, assisted villages, entrepreneurship training, and mentoring marginalized people to mustahiq while LazisMu PDM Surakarta City through the Economic Empowerment Program including Aisyiyah Family Economic Development (Bu-Eka) and business carts. LazisMu UMS has distributed its productive zakat funds, including providing goods or equipment assistance to mustahiq/people who support their entrepreneurial fields, while LazisMu PDM Surakarta City also provides in the form of creative productive in the form of financial assistance or equipment in the field of entrepreneurship.

title: Economic Empowerment of Small Businesses Through Zakat Funds at the Amil Zakat Infaq Shadaqah Institute in Surakarta
abstract: This study examines the management and impact of zakat fund distribution on the economic empowerment of small business communities by the Amil Zakat Infaq Shadaqah Institute (LazisMu) in Surakarta. Employing a qualitative field research approach, data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation involving LazisMu administrators and small business recipients. The findings reveal that zakat funds are allocated to underprivileged individuals with entrepreneurial potential, based on recommendations and thorough assessments. LazisMu implements various empowerment programs, including direct business capital assistance, entrepreneurship training, mentoring, and provision of equipment or financial support tailored to the needs of mustahiq. Notable initiatives such as the By Friend and By Request programs at LazisMu UMS and the Economic Empowerment Program at LazisMu PDM Surakarta City have contributed to increased business capacity and sustainability among beneficiaries. The study concludes that effective zakat fund management and targeted empowerment strategies play a significant role in enhancing the welfare and independence of small business actors, thereby fostering broader community economic development in Surakarta.

title: Enablers and Inhibitors of Business-IT Alignment
abstract: This paper provides insight into identifying areas that help or hinder business-IT alignment. Alignment focuses on the activities that management performs to achieve cohesive goals across the organization. The aim of this paper is to determine the most important enablers and inhibitors to alignment. The paper presents and analyzes the results of a multi-year study of strategic alignment. Data were obtained from business and information technology executives from over 500 firms representing 15 industries who attended classes addressing alignment at IBM’s Advanced Business Institute. The executives were asked to describe those activities that assist in achieving alignment and those which seem to hinder it. These enablers and inhibitors to alignment were then analyzed with respect to industry, to time, and executive position. The results indicate that certain activities can assist in the achievement of this state of alignment while others are clearly barriers. Achieving alignment is evolutionary and dynamic.
