title: Enablers and Inhibitors of Business-IT Alignment
abstract: This study investigates the key enablers and inhibitors of business-IT alignment through a multi-year empirical analysis involving over 1,000 executives from more than 500 firms across 15 industries. Drawing on survey data, interviews, and consulting observations collected between 1992 and 1997 at IBM’s Advanced Business Institute, the research identifies senior executive support, IT involvement in strategy development, mutual understanding between IT and business, strong partnerships, well-prioritized IT projects, and IT leadership as primary enablers of alignment. Conversely, lack of close IT-business relationships, poor prioritization, unmet commitments, insufficient business understanding by IT, lack of executive support for IT, and weak IT leadership are found to be major inhibitors. The findings reveal that these factors are consistent across industries, time periods, and executive roles, underscoring the evolutionary and dynamic nature of alignment. The study validates prior anecdotal evidence and emphasizes that maximizing enablers while minimizing inhibitors is essential for achieving effective business-IT alignment.
venue: Communications of the Association for Information Systems

title: Exploring transparency: a new framework for responsible business management
abstract: Purpose – The purpose of this paper is to critically review the relevant literature on transparency, provide a comprehensive definition of transparency, and present a new framework for facilitating the adoption of transparency as an ethical cornerstone and pragmatic strategy for organizational responsible business management. Design/methodology/approach – A systematic literature review – a methodology adopted from medical sciences to eliminate research bias – was conducted. In doing so, the definitions, antecedents, and consequences of transparency are accessed and synthesized. Findings – Based upon this process transparency is defined as the extent to which a stakeholder perceives an organization provides learning opportunities about itself. A conceptual framework emerged from the data. It describes when transparency is especially important, what organizations can do to be more transparent, and the potential benefits of transparency. Practical implications – The transparency framework can be used as a guide for organizations attempting to change their behavior, image, and performance by adopting transparency as a value in their organization. In addition, the framework can be used to create and adopt a universal (i.e. industry-wide or even societal-wide) code of conduct. Furthermore, this review, definition, and framework provide a template for academics to advance transparency theory, and empirically test the construct’s application. Originality/value – As a new research field, transparency has lacked a concise definition as well as a conceptual framework. This is the first comprehensive summary of transparency. In addition, this study contributes to the methodology of evaluating construct definitions to advance empirical research.

title: Exploring transparency: a new framework for responsible business management
abstract: This paper critically examines the concept of transparency in business management by conducting a systematic literature review to address inconsistencies and ambiguities in existing definitions. The authors synthesize prior research to propose a comprehensive definition of transparency as the extent to which stakeholders perceive an organization provides learning opportunities about itself. Building on this definition, the study introduces a new conceptual framework that identifies when transparency is most critical, outlines organizational strategies for enhancing transparency, and highlights its potential benefits, particularly in fostering trust and ethical decision making. The framework serves as both a practical guide for organizations seeking to embed transparency as a core value and a foundation for developing universal codes of conduct. Additionally, the paper contributes methodological insights for evaluating construct definitions, thereby advancing empirical research on transparency and responsible business management.

title: Factors Affecting Business Success of Small & Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Thailand
abstract: This study attempted to identify factors that are affecting business success of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Thailand. The intention of this study is to provide the understanding on how people should start their business by looking at all the factors affecting business success hence help to reduce the risk of failure and increase chances of success. The study examined eight factors that influence the SMEs business success. These factors are: SMEs characteristic, management and know-how, products and services, Customer and Market, the way of doing business and cooperation, resources and finance, Strategy, and external environment. The theoretical framework has been drawn out and questionnaire was designed based on the factors chosen. Eight hypotheses were developed to find out factors that are affecting Business Success of SMEs in Thailand. The entire hypotheses were successfully tested with SPSS and five hypotheses were accepted. The regression analysis result shown that the most significant factors affecting business success of SMEs in Thailand were SMEs characteristics, customer and market, the way of doing business, resources and finance, and external environment.

title: Factors Affecting Business Success of Small & Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Thailand
abstract: This study investigates the key factors influencing the business success of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Thailand, aiming to provide insights that can help entrepreneurs reduce failure risks and enhance their chances of success. Drawing on a theoretical framework and survey data, the research examines eight potential determinants: SME characteristics, management know-how, products and services, customer and market orientation, business practices and cooperation, resources and finance, strategy, and external environment. Using regression analysis on responses from Thai SMEs, the study finds that SME characteristics, customer and market factors, business practices, resources and finance, and the external environment are the most significant contributors to business success. The findings highlight the multifaceted nature of SME performance in Thailand and offer practical implications for policymakers and business owners seeking to foster sustainable growth in this vital sector.

title: Flexibility and Resilience in Corporate Decision Making: A New Sustainability-Based Risk Management System in Uncertain Times
abstract: Risk management plays a key role in uncertain times, preventing corporations from acting rashly and incorrectly, allowing them to become flexible and resilient. A global turbulence such as the COVID-19 pandemic has had a strong impact on individual companies and entire economic sectors, raising the question of whether a paradigm shift is necessary, in order to enable a new cycle of development that is much environmentally, socially and economically sustainable. This environmental and socio-economic context of profound uncertainty forces organizations to consider more carefully the risk factors affecting their business continuity, as well as how these factors relate to sustainability issues. However, there is a gap in knowledge about how risk management systems relate to sustainability management systems, and how both of them exert influence on business performance, especially from a theoretical point of view. The aim of this study is to address this gap, by developing a new interpretative framework for the analysis of risk management strategies in organizations. This approach has been identified in economic hermeneutics as an innovative methodological tool to improve the knowledge of risk and design the most appropriate management strategies. The paper provides two main results: the first one is the construction of a theoretical model that relates risk management to sustainability management; the second one is an operational framework of multidimensional risk assessment useful for analysis at different levels (business, competitive scenario and system). Finally, the model also makes it possible to carry out a sustainability assessment through risk evaluation in the perspective of the sustainable development goals.
venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management

title: Flexibility and Resilience in Corporate Decision Making: A New Sustainability-Based Risk Management System in Uncertain Times
abstract: This study addresses the growing need for integrated approaches to risk management and sustainability in corporate decision-making, particularly in the context of heightened uncertainty exemplified by crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Through a hybrid analytical and empirical methodology, the research develops a novel interpretative framework that connects risk management systems with sustainability management, drawing on economic hermeneutics to enhance organizational flexibility and resilience. The paper constructs a theoretical model linking risk and sustainability, and proposes an operational multidimensional risk assessment framework applicable at business, sectoral, and systemic levels. Empirical validation using a case study from the ceramics industry demonstrates the model's utility in both retrospective and prospective scenario analysis. The findings highlight the importance of integrating technical and strategic perspectives in risk management to support sustainable development goals, offering organizations a competitive lever for sustainable growth in volatile environments.
venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management

title: Green supply chain management practices and performance
abstract: Purpose – The purpose of this study is to examine the deployment of pro‐active and re‐active practices in the implementation of green supply chain management (GSCM) and analyze their impact on environmental, economic, and intangible performance by considering business strategy as organizational focus.Design/methodology/approach – Data were collected from a sample of 190 ISO 14001 certified manufacturing companies in Thailand and used to test the research hypotheses. Factor analysis was used to examine the construct validity while multivariate linear regression was used to test criteria validity.Findings – The threat of legislation and regulation (re‐active practices) was a consideration that resulted in companies enhancing their environmental, economic, and intangible performance. Reverse logistics practices (pro‐active practices) had low levels of adoption and do not have a significant impact on GSCM performance.Research limitations/implications – This study did not consider some aspects of organizationa...

title: Green supply chain management practices and performance
abstract: This study investigates the influence of pro-active and re-active green supply chain management (GSCM) practices on environmental, economic, and intangible performance outcomes in ISO 14001 certified manufacturing firms in Thailand, with business strategy as a contextual variable. Using survey data from 190 companies, factor analysis and multivariate linear regression were employed to validate constructs and test hypotheses. Findings reveal that re-active practices driven by legislative and regulatory pressures significantly enhance all dimensions of performance, while pro-active practices such as reverse logistics show low adoption rates and lack significant impact on GSCM performance. The study highlights the potential negative consequences of a low-cost strategy on GSCM investment and underscores the importance of considering both institutional drivers and business strategy in GSCM implementation. By focusing on an emerging economy context and including intangible performance measures, this research contributes novel insights to the literature on sustainable supply chain management.

title: Human and Financial Capital for Microenterprise Development: Evidence from a Field and Lab Experiment
abstract: Microenterprises constitute an important source of employment, and developing such enterprises is a key policy concern in most countries. But what is the most efficient tool for microenterprise development? We study this question in a developing country context Tanzania, where microenterprises are the source of employment for more than half of the labor force, and we report from a field experiment that jointly investigated the importance of a human capital intervention business training and a financial capital intervention business grant. Using data from three survey rounds, a lab experiment, and administrative records of the microfinance institution, we present evidence on business performance, management practices, happiness, business knowledge, and noncognitive abilities. Our study demonstrates strong effects of the combination of the two interventions on male entrepreneurs, while the effects on female entrepreneurs are much more muted. The results suggest that long-term finance is an important constraint for microfinance entrepreneurs, but that business training is essential to transform financial capital into productive investments. Our study also points to the need for more comprehensive measures to promote the businesses of female entrepreneurs. Data, as supplemental material, are available at http://dx.doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2014.1933 . This paper was accepted by John List, behavioral economics.

title: Human and Financial Capital for Microenterprise Development: Evidence from a Field and Lab Experiment
abstract: This study investigates the relative importance of human and financial capital constraints for microenterprise development through a randomized field experiment in Tanzania, complemented by a lab experiment. Microentrepreneurs were randomly assigned to receive either business training, a business grant, or no intervention. The results show that business training significantly increased profits and sales among male entrepreneurs, primarily through the adoption of improved business practices, while having limited effects for female entrepreneurs. In contrast, the business grant had no measurable impact on business outcomes for either gender. The lab experiment reveals that training enhanced business knowledge and shifted mind-set for both men and women, narrowing gender gaps in risk attitudes and self-confidence, though women remained less willing to compete. These findings suggest that human capital is a more binding constraint than financial capital for microenterprise growth, particularly for men, and highlight the need for tailored interventions to address persistent gender disparities in entrepreneurial outcomes.

title: Information overload in the information age: a review of the literature from business administration, business psychology, and related disciplines with a bibliometric approach and framework development
abstract: In the light of the information age, information overload research in new areas (e.g., social media, virtual collaboration) rises rapidly in many fields of research in business administration with a variety of methods and subjects. This review article analyzes the development of information overload literature in business administration and related interdisciplinary fields and provides a comprehensive and overarching overview using a bibliometric literature analysis combined with a snowball sampling approach. For the last decade, this article reveals research directions and bridges of literature in a wide range of fields of business administration (e.g., accounting, finance, health management, human resources, innovation management, international management, information systems, marketing, manufacturing, or organizational science). This review article identifies the major papers of various research streams to capture the pulse of the information overload-related research and suggest new questions that could be addressed in the future and identifies concrete open gaps for further research. Furthermore, this article presents a new framework for structuring information overload issues which extends our understanding of influence factors and effects of information overload in the decision-making process.

title: Information overload in the information age: a review of the literature from business administration, business psychology, and related disciplines with a bibliometric approach and framework development
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive literature review of information overload in the context of the information age, focusing on business administration, business psychology, and related disciplines. Employing a bibliometric analysis combined with snowball sampling, the study examines research published between 2004 and 2017 to map the development, key themes, and interdisciplinary connections within information overload scholarship. The review identifies major research streams across diverse fields such as accounting, finance, health management, human resources, innovation management, international management, information systems, marketing, manufacturing, and organizational science. It highlights the resurgence of interest in information overload due to technological advancements and the proliferation of digital information sources. The paper addresses gaps in previous reviews by integrating insights from multiple disciplines and providing a structured overview of theoretical foundations and methodological approaches. Additionally, it introduces a novel framework that delineates the influence factors and effects of information overload throughout the decision-making process. The findings underscore persistent challenges in managing information load and propose directions for future research to better understand and mitigate the impact of information overload in organizational settings.

title: Information Production and Capital Allocation: Decentralized vs. Hierarchical Firms
abstract: This paper assesses different organizational forms in terms of their ability to generate information about investment projects and allocate capital to these projects efficiently. A decentralized approach with small, single-manager firms is most likely to be attractive when information about individual projects is soft' and cannot be credibly transmitted. Moreover, holding fixed firm size, soft information also favors flatter organizations with fewer layers of management. In contrast, large hierarchical firms with multiple layers of management are at a comparative advantage when information can be costlessly hardened' and passed along within the hierarchy. As a concrete application of the theory, the paper discusses the consequences of consolidation in the banking industry. It has been documented that when large banks acquire small banks, there is a pronounced decline in lending to small businesses. To the extent that small-business lending relies heavily on soft information, this is exactly what the theory would lead one to expect.

title: Information Production and Capital Allocation: Decentralized vs. Hierarchical Firms
abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework to compare decentralized and hierarchical organizational structures in their effectiveness at producing information and allocating capital among investment projects. The analysis highlights that decentralized firms, characterized by single managers with local authority, are better suited for environments where project evaluation relies on “soft” information—information that is difficult to verify or transmit credibly within a hierarchy. In such settings, decentralization enhances research incentives and leads to more efficient capital allocation within units, though it may limit flexibility in reallocating resources across units. Conversely, hierarchical firms with multiple management layers have a comparative advantage when information can be “hardened” and easily communicated up the chain, enabling both efficient cross-unit capital reallocation and stronger research incentives through advocacy for resources. The model also predicts that, when soft information predominates but firm size must remain large, flatter organizational structures are preferable. As an application, the paper examines bank consolidation and its impact on small-business lending, arguing that the observed decline in such lending following mergers is consistent with the theory: large hierarchical banks are less effective at utilizing soft information critical for small-business credit decisions. The findings provide insight into the trade-offs between organizational design, information production, and capital allocation efficiency.

title: Life Cycle Assessment as Entrepreneurial Tool for Business Management and Green Innovations
abstract: A transition for a green economy has encouraged companies to use new tools which promote internal corporate entrepreneurship, increase the competitiveness and achieve sustainable results. This article presented a theoretical discussion of how the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) can presents as an entrepreneurial tool for modern business management and green innovation. Studies of LCA were analyzed showing benefits and applications in the areas of strategic planning, production, process of development of products, search and development, social and environmental responsibility, and marketing. As for green innovations, there were analyzed studies of innovations in products, processes and services. The tool assists in making sustainable decisions, fortifies the management of the business processes, the management of operations and the promotion of greener innovations.

title: Life Cycle Assessment as Entrepreneurial Tool for Business Management and Green Innovations
abstract: This paper explores the role of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) as an entrepreneurial tool for business management and the advancement of green innovations. Through a theoretical analysis supported by recent studies, the research demonstrates how LCA facilitates sustainable decision-making and enhances competitiveness by integrating environmental considerations across product, process, and service life cycles. The study highlights LCA’s applications in strategic planning, product development, operations management, and corporate social responsibility, emphasizing its value in fostering internal corporate entrepreneurship and driving green innovation. By adopting LCA, firms can better identify opportunities for environmental improvement, support sustainable business practices, and create value through innovation, positioning themselves for success in a transitioning green economy.

title: Measurement of Business Economic Performance: An Examination of Method Convergence
abstract: Strategic management researchers have measured business economic performance (BEP) through either perceptual assessments of senior executives or secondary data sources, but few explicitly evaluate the degree of convergence across methods. In an effort to examine method convergence, we collected data on three dimensions-sales growth, net income growth, and profitability (ROI) using both methods. Although convergent and discriminant validity were achieved using Campbell and Fiske's Multi Trait, Multi Method (MTMM) and Confiratory Factor Analysis (CFA), the approaches yielded different insights. The advantages of CFA over MTMM is demonstrated with implications for strategy research.

title: Measurement of Business Economic Performance: An Examination of Method Convergence
abstract: This study investigates the convergence among alternative methods used to measure business economic performance, addressing concerns about the comparability and validity of different approaches. Using a sample of business units, the research examines the extent to which commonly employed financial and composite performance measures yield consistent results. The analysis reveals significant, but not complete, convergence among various measurement methods, highlighting both overlaps and discrepancies in performance assessments. The findings underscore the importance of method selection in empirical research and suggest that reliance on a single measure may lead to incomplete or biased conclusions. Implications for future research and managerial practice are discussed, emphasizing the need for multi-method approaches in evaluating business economic performance.

title: METHODICAL APPROACH TO THE CHOICE OF A BUSINESS MANAGEMENT STRATEGY WITHIN THE FRAMEWORK OF A CHANGE IN COMMERCIAL ACTIVITIES
abstract: The main purpose of the article is the formation of new strategies in business management with changes in commercial activities. The object of the study is the system of commercial activity and possible changes in it. The scientific task is the definition of a new methodological approach to the formation of new strategies in business management with changes in commercial activity. The research methodology involves the use of a modern method for modeling strategies in business management with changes in business activities. As a result, we presented a methodical approach to the formation of business management strategies in the face of changes in commercial activities. The author’s vision of how the stages of forming the main business management strategy through block-object-oriented modeling should look graphically and schematically was presented. Each of its blocks involves many processions and actions aimed at changes in commercial activity. The innovative novelty of our study lies in the presented methodological approach to the formation of a business management strategy within the framework of changes in commercial activity.

title: METHODICAL APPROACH TO THE CHOICE OF A BUSINESS MANAGEMENT STRATEGY WITHIN THE FRAMEWORK OF A CHANGE IN COMMERCIAL ACTIVITIES
abstract: This study presents a methodical approach to selecting business management strategies in the context of changing commercial activities. Recognizing the dynamic and unpredictable nature of modern business environments, the research focuses on developing a systematic framework that enables enterprises to effectively manage strategic changes and maintain competitiveness. The proposed methodology utilizes block-object-oriented modeling to structure the stages of strategy formation, ensuring that each phase incorporates processes and actions responsive to both internal and external change drivers. By integrating literature review, trend analysis, and practical modeling techniques, the study offers a comprehensive tool for managers to assess readiness for change, align strategic decisions with organizational goals, and adapt to evolving market conditions. The novelty of this research lies in its structured, process-oriented approach to strategy selection, which enhances the capacity of enterprises to implement effective change management within commercial activities.

title: Re-Imagining the Morality of Management: A Modern Virtue Ethics Approach
abstract: In this paper the problematic nature of the morality of management, in particular related to business organisations operating under Anglo-American capitalism, is explored. MacIntyre’s critique of managers in After Virtue (1985) serves as the starting point but this critique is itself subjected to analysis leading to a more balanced and contemporary view of the morality of management than MacIntyre provides. Paradoxically perhaps, MacIntyre’s own virtues-goods-practice-institution schema is shown to provide a way of re-imagining business organisations and management and thereby holds out the possibility of resolving the issue of the morality of management within such organisations. Implications for management practice are drawn out.

title: Re-Imagining the Morality of Management: A Modern Virtue Ethics Approach
abstract: This paper critically examines the morality of management within business organizations operating under Anglo-American capitalism, using Alasdair MacIntyre’s critique of managerial roles as a foundation. While MacIntyre’s influential argument in After Virtue characterizes managers as embodiments of emotivism and moral neutrality, this analysis contends that his critique requires both tempering and updating in light of contemporary debates on bureaucracy and management ethics. The paper reviews responses to MacIntyre, highlighting the ongoing moral ambiguities faced by managers in complex organizational environments. It then re-engages with MacIntyre’s own virtues-goods-practice-institution schema, arguing that this framework offers a constructive means to re-imagine the morality of management by embedding ethical practices within organizational life. The implications for management practice are explored, suggesting that a modern virtue ethics approach can address persistent concerns about manipulation, compartmentalization, and moral responsibility in managerial roles, ultimately providing a more substantive and hopeful account of ethical management.

title: Response Rates in Business and Management Research: An Overview of Current Practice and Suggestions for Future Direction
abstract: This paper examines response rates (RR) in published research in business and management journals. Its aim is to evaluate the efficacy of RR-enhancing strategies, explore differences in RR between sub-disciplines and geographical regions, provide a critical appraisal of RR in business and management research, and offer guidelines for assessing and improving RR in business and management research. Data are analysed from 1093 survey-based papers published between 2009 and 2013 in a representative sample of business and management journals. The results of the study are discussed, and their implications for RR in business and management research are provided.

title: Response Rates in Business and Management Research: An Overview of Current Practice and Suggestions for Future Direction
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive overview of response rates (RR) in business and management research, critically examining current practices and offering guidance for future studies. Drawing on a review of 1,093 survey-based articles from leading journals, the study highlights the persistent decline in RR and the lack of consensus on acceptable thresholds, noting that standards vary widely across disciplines, regions, and subfields. The analysis evaluates the effectiveness of commonly recommended strategies to enhance RR, such as Dillman’s Total Design Method, personalization, pre-notification, follow-ups, incentives, and survey design considerations. Findings indicate mixed evidence regarding the impact of these techniques and underscore inconsistent adherence to best practices in reporting and improving RR. The paper concludes by proposing informed baselines for evaluating RR adequacy rather than rigid benchmarks, aiming to assist authors, reviewers, and editors in making informed judgments about survey quality. Recommendations for future research include greater transparency in reporting RR procedures and outcomes, as well as further investigation into context-specific factors influencing participation in business and management surveys.

title: Should Investors Bet on the Jockey or the Horse? Evidence from the Evolution of Firms from Early Business Plans to Public Companies
abstract: We study how firm characteristics evolve from early business plan to initial public offering (IPO) to public company for 50 venture capital (VC)-financed companies. Firm business lines remain remarkably stable while management turnover is substantial. Management turnover is positively related to alienable asset formation. We obtain similar results using all 2004 IPOs, suggesting that our main results are not specific to VC-backed firms or the time period. The results suggest that, at the margin, investors in start-ups should place more weight on the business (“the horse”) than on the management team (“the jockey”). The results also inform theories of the firm.

title: Should Investors Bet on the Jockey or the Horse? Evidence from the Evolution of Firms from Early Business Plans to Public Companies
abstract: This study examines the evolution of 50 venture capital-financed firms from early business plans through IPO to public company status, focusing on the stability of business lines and management turnover. The findings reveal that while firms’ core business lines remain largely unchanged throughout their development, there is significant turnover in top management, particularly among CEOs and founders. Management changes are more frequent in firms with greater alienable assets at inception. These patterns persist in a broader sample of all 2004 IPOs, indicating the results are not unique to VC-backed firms or a specific era. The evidence suggests that investors should prioritize the underlying business model (“the horse”) over the initial management team (“the jockey”) when evaluating start-ups. The study also discusses implications for theories of the firm, highlighting the early emergence and persistence of non-human assets as critical resources and questioning claims about the increasing importance of human capital in new firms.

title: Small Business Uniqueness and the Theory of Financial Management
abstract: Small businesses do not share the same financial management problems with large businesses. This paper shows that the source of the differences could be traced to several characteristics unique to small businesses. This uniqueness in turn creates a whole new set of financial management issues. The major implication is that, yes, there are new and interesting topics in small business financial management research.

title: Small Business Uniqueness and the Theory of Financial Management
abstract: This paper examines the distinct characteristics of small businesses and their implications for financial management theory. Unlike large firms, small businesses typically lack access to public capital markets, have undiversified owner portfolios, face ineffective or absent limited liability, and are often managed by entrepreneurial founders with incomplete management teams. These features result in higher costs associated with market imperfections, informal relationships with stakeholders, and flexible compensation schemes. The analysis demonstrates that such uniqueness generates financial management issues that differ fundamentally from those encountered by large firms, particularly in areas such as agency problems, information asymmetry, and transaction costs. The paper argues that existing corporate finance theory does not fully address these challenges and calls for the development of a new paradigm tailored to small business financial management. Implications for future research include the need to explore alternative financial arrangements, governance structures, and decision-making processes that reflect the realities of small business operations.

title: Strategic issues in customer relationship management (CRM) implementation
abstract: The number of customer relationship management (CRM) implementations has grown dramatically in recent years. However, few academic studies of the issues associated with the implementation of the concept are available. This paper offers a modest contribution through the analysis of a case study of a CRM implementation at a UK‐based manufacturing company. The case study illustrates that CRM is a complex and holistic concept, organised around business processes and the integration of information technologies. The study also highlights that implementing CRM requires effective leadership, sourcing, targeting and evaluation strategies.

title: Strategic issues in customer relationship management (CRM) implementation
abstract: This paper examines the strategic issues involved in implementing customer relationship management (CRM) systems, drawing on a case study of a UK-based manufacturing company. The study highlights the complexity and holistic nature of CRM, emphasizing its integration with business processes and information technologies. Key findings indicate that successful CRM implementation requires strong leadership, clear sourcing strategies, effective customer targeting, and robust evaluation mechanisms. The research underscores the importance of aligning technological and business objectives, managing organizational change, and adopting a customer-centric approach. The paper concludes by identifying gaps in existing literature and recommending further empirical research to better understand the critical factors influencing CRM success.

title: Strategic knowledge management: theory, practice and future challenges
abstract: The current knowledge economy requires companies to create new business structures and new concepts for the management of its resources to remain competitive. The latest approaches to strategic management (Ferreira et al., 2016) tend to consider strategic alliances (as sources of knowledge) and intellectual capital (human, structural and relational capital) as the main sources for a sustainable competitive advantage. In an increasingly globalized world, the survival of business management depends on their organizational intelligence, which is the result of information and knowledge systems they have, the skills of its employees and how they relate to its stakeholders (Durst and Edvardsson, 2012).

title: Strategic knowledge management: theory, practice and future challenges
abstract: This editorial introduces the special issue on strategic knowledge management (SKM), highlighting its theoretical foundations, practical applications, and emerging challenges in the context of the knowledge economy. The issue explores SKM as a critical organizational capability encompassing knowledge creation, organization, transfer, and application to achieve sustainable competitive advantage. Drawing on resource-based and knowledge-based views of the firm, the editorial discusses key concepts such as intellectual capital, absorptive capacity, and dynamic capabilities, emphasizing the interplay between technological and intellectual resources for organizational survival. The special issue presents a collection of empirical and theoretical studies employing diverse methodologies to examine innovative SKM practices across various organizational contexts and cultures. Featured articles address topics such as internal and external search strategies for innovation, dual relational embeddedness in multinational corporations, and holistic models for inter-plant knowledge transfer. Collectively, these contributions advance understanding of how SKM drives competitiveness and innovation while identifying future research directions to address the complexities of managing knowledge in rapidly evolving business environments.

title: Strategy and Human Resource Management
abstract: How is human resource management (HRM) strategic to a firm's viability and how might it help to lay a basis for sustained competitive advantage? How can managers pursue their goals for labour productivity and organisational flexibility in socially acceptable ways? This book explores such questions. The authors develop a conceptual framework to provide an exploration of the growing field of strategic HRM. This text should be of interest to MBA students and advanced undergraduate and postgraduate students of HRM. It should also be an valuable resource for anyone interested in the role of HRM in business success.

title: Strategy and Human Resource Management
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive and critical analysis of the strategic role of human resource management (HRM) in organizational success, integrating research and practice to offer an accessible and engaging account for students, scholars, and practitioners. Building on the strengths of its previous edition, it introduces an expanded discussion of HRM goals, a new typology of HR systems, and fresh insights into organizational culture, climate, and the unique challenges faced by service organizations and the public sector. The work synthesizes the latest developments in strategic HRM, encouraging readers to critically evaluate how human resources contribute to business performance and competitive advantage. By bridging theoretical frameworks with practical examples, the paper serves as an essential resource for understanding and applying strategic HRM within the context of broader organizational strategy.

title: Student Centric Curriculum Design and Implementation – Challenges & Opportunities in Business Management & IT Education
abstract: Student-centric curriculum design and implementation in higher education system are getting importance due to the reason of creating employable and skilled graduates who can take optimum decisions for industry problems and who can lead technocrat society. Even though student-centric curriculum is essential in all areas of higher education, it became essential in business management and information technology due to the fact that these areas are changing at a faster rate due to the enhanced competition in globalized business. In this paper, we have discussed the challenges and opportunities in curriculum planning, designing, and effective implementation in autonomous and affiliated business schools. We have discussed the possibility of designing industry oriented curriculum in business management and information technology, which contain both industry and research experience components. This student centric curriculum improvement model will take care of rapid growth of both the fields and the requirement of updating the curriculum with present developments. The opportunities and challenges of student-centric curriculum design and developments in Business management subject and in Information technology subjects are discussed. The advantages, benefits, constraints, and disadvantages of such system are listed. Though the implementation of the new model is challenging, the advantages and the benefits outlay the disadvantages and the constraints.

title: Student Centric Curriculum Design and Implementation – Challenges & Opportunities in Business Management & IT Education
abstract: This paper examines the growing significance of student-centric curriculum design and implementation in higher education, with a focus on business management and information technology disciplines. Rapid changes in these fields, driven by globalization and technological advancement, necessitate curricula that are responsive to industry needs and foster both knowledge acquisition and research skills among students. The study analyzes the challenges faced by autonomous and affiliated institutions in planning, designing, and executing such curricula, including aligning course content with industry requirements, integrating research components, and adopting innovative pedagogical approaches. Opportunities arising from student-centric models are explored, particularly their potential to enhance employability, adaptability, and leadership capabilities among graduates. The paper also presents an ABCD (Advantages, Benefits, Constraints, Disadvantages) analysis of student-centric curriculum models, highlighting that while implementation poses significant challenges—such as resource constraints and resistance to change—the overall benefits outweigh the drawbacks. The findings underscore the importance of continuous curriculum development to keep pace with evolving industry standards and advocate for collaborative efforts between academia and industry to ensure relevance and effectiveness in business management and IT education.

title: The Business of Sport Management
abstract: The scale and importance of the lucrative sport industry demands quality business professionals. This ground-breaking new book equips the manager and future manager of sport organisations with the tools they need to deliver. The Business of Sport Management is ideal for students of sports management on programmes of leisure studies, sports studies and business studies. Written and contributed to by leading academics and practitioners in UK, Europe and Australia it is also of great interest to practitioners working in sport businesses.  Blending both theory and practice The Business of Sports Management looks at the distinctive context of sport organisations. It then looks at management theories and practice within the functional areas such as finance, human resource management and marketing. Finally it considers contemporary issues of importance such as sponsorship and endorsement, risk management and the media. Set in an international environment the authors have been careful to choose stimulating examples from a wide variety of sports.

title: The Business of Sport Management
abstract: This review critically examines The Business of Sport Management, edited by John Beech and Simon Chadwick, highlighting its comprehensive and engaging approach to the evolving field of sport management. The book distinguishes itself by moving beyond the typical reliance on American case studies, offering a global perspective and integrating humor to enhance accessibility. Contributions from twenty diverse authors cover the historical progression from amateurism to commercialism, address contemporary issues such as player contracts, e-business strategies, and legal considerations, and consistently link theory to real-world examples. While the text occasionally presents contradictory viewpoints and could benefit from additional operational insights, it effectively challenges readers to apply concepts and anticipate industry trends. The final chapters provide forward-looking analysis on the future of sport business, emphasizing innovation, customer engagement, and brand diversification. Overall, the book is recommended as an essential resource for students and practitioners seeking both theoretical grounding and practical guidance in sport management.

title: The challenges and opportunities of a global health crisis: the management and business implications of COVID-19 from an Asian perspective
abstract: On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the coronavirus (COVID-19) outbreak a pandemic. As the evolution and implications of the COVID-19 crisis are still unfolding, we posit that exploring the experiences and strategic responses of Asian countries may shed light on ways to combat COVID-19 for the rest of the world. In this paper, we first articulate the importance of resilience, strategic agility, and entrepreneurship in the context of the fight against COVID-19. Then, with the focus on China, South Korea, and Singapore, we discuss the impact COVID-19 is having on economies and businesses, governmental support for businesses and societies, and implications for global supply chain disruptions. We hope that the global health system will recover quickly, and that the world economy will be revitalized with the contributions and collaboration of science (including social science), industry, and governments.

title: The challenges and opportunities of a global health crisis: the management and business implications of COVID-19 from an Asian perspective
abstract: This paper examines the management and business implications of the COVID-19 pandemic from an Asian perspective, focusing on China, South Korea, and Singapore. It explores how resilience, strategic agility, and entrepreneurship have shaped responses to the crisis at individual, organizational, and governmental levels. The study highlights the significant economic disruptions and challenges to global supply chains while also identifying opportunities for innovation, industry transformation, and new business models. Governmental support measures and cross-sector collaborations are analyzed as critical factors in mitigating negative impacts and fostering recovery. The findings suggest that Asian experiences offer valuable lessons for enhancing crisis management capabilities and leveraging opportunities in the face of global health emergencies.

title: The Effectiveness of Business Codes: A Critical Examination of Existing Studies and the Development of an Integrated Research Model
abstract: Business codes are a widely used management instrument. Research into the effectiveness of business codes has, however, produced conflicting results. The main reasons for the divergent findings are: varying definitions of key terms; deficiencies in the empirical data and methodologies used; and a lack of theory. In this paper, we propose an integrated research model and suggest directions for future research.

title: The Effectiveness of Business Codes: A Critical Examination of Existing Studies and the Development of an Integrated Research Model
abstract: This paper critically examines the existing body of research on the effectiveness of business codes, highlighting significant inconsistencies in findings due to divergent definitions, methodological limitations, and a lack of theoretical grounding. Through a comprehensive review of conceptual and empirical studies, the authors identify key sources of confusion, such as varying interpretations of what constitutes a business code and differences in research design. To address these challenges, the paper offers a clarified definition of business codes and proposes an integrated research model to better assess their impact on organizational behavior and outcomes. The study concludes by outlining directions for future research that emphasize the need for greater conceptual clarity, improved empirical methodologies, and a more robust theoretical framework to advance understanding of how business codes influence ethical conduct within organizations.

title: The Evolution of the Corporate Social Performance Model
abstract: This paper traces the evolution of the corporate social performance model by focusing on three challenges to the concept of corporate social responsibility: economic responsibility, public responsibility, and social responsiveness, it also examines social issues management as a dimension of corporate social performance. It concludes that the corporate social performance model is valuable for business and society study and that it provides the beginnings of a paradigm for the field.

title: The Evolution of the Corporate Social Performance Model
abstract: This paper examines the historical development and conceptual refinement of the corporate social performance (CSP) model, highlighting its evolution through scholarly debate on corporate social responsibility (CSR). By analyzing three major challenges—economic responsibility, public responsibility, and social responsiveness—the authors demonstrate how the CSP model integrates these perspectives into a multidimensional framework that encompasses principles of responsibility, processes of responsiveness, and policies for managing social issues. The paper argues that this integrative approach addresses critiques of CSR by recognizing both economic imperatives and societal expectations, positioning CSP as a valuable analytical tool for understanding the dynamic relationship between business and society. Ultimately, the CSP model is presented as a foundational paradigm for future research in business and society, reflecting the ongoing negotiation between corporate obligations and evolving societal values.

title: The impact of ERP systems on firm and business process performance
abstract: Purpose – The purpose of this article is to provide further insights into the adoption of enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems and the impacts on organisational performance. It aims at challenging existing claims of ERP vendors with regard to the benefits of their products and at providing evidence of the benefits of bundling ERPS with supply chain management systems.Design/methodology/approach – A survey was conducted to collect data on several aspects of organisational performance in companies that adopted ERPS and/or SCMS and the respective control groups. Financial key performance indicators were used to measure overall firm performance and the supply‐chain operations reference model to operationalise performance at the business process (supply chain) level.Findings – The key results contradict the claims of ERPS vendors insofar as no significant performance differences were found between ERPS adopters and non‐adopters, either at the business process level, or at the overall firm level. title: The impact of ERP systems on firm and business process performance
abstract: This study investigates the impact of enterprise resource planning systems (ERPS) on firm-level and business process performance, challenging vendor claims regarding ERPS benefits and examining the additional effect of integrating supply chain management systems (SCMS). Using survey data from firms that have adopted ERPS, SCMS, and control groups, the research employs financial key performance indicators for overall firm performance and the Supply-Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) model for business process performance. The findings reveal no significant differences in performance between ERPS adopters and non-adopters at either the firm or business process level. However, firms with longer ERPS experience demonstrate improved overall performance, though not at the business process level. Notably, only firms adopting both ERPS and SCMS achieve significantly higher business process performance, suggesting that the integration of SCMS is critical for realizing operational benefits. These results question the standalone value of ERPS and highlight the importance of complementary systems in enhancing business process outcomes.

title: The Reservoir model and architecture for open federated cloud computing
abstract: The emerging cloud-computing paradigm is rapidly gaining momentum as an alternative to traditional IT (information technology). However, contemporary cloud-computing offerings are primarily targeted for Web 2.0-style applications. Only recently have they begun to address the requirements of enterprise solutions, such as support for infrastructure service-level agreements. To address the challenges and deficiencies in the current state of the art, we propose a modular, extensible cloud architecture with intrinsic support for business service management and the federation of clouds. The goal is to facilitate an open, service-based online economy in which resources and services are transparently provisioned and managed across clouds on an ondemand basis at competitive costs with high-quality service. The Reservoir project is motivated by the vision of implementing an architecture that would enable providers of cloud infrastructure to dynamically partner with each other to create a seemingly infinite pool of IT resources while fully preserving their individual autonomy in making technological and business management decisions. To this end, Reservoir could leverage and extend the advantages of virtualization and embed autonomous management in the infrastructure. At the same time, the Reservoir approach aims to achieve a very ambitious goal: creating a foundation for next-generation enterprise-grade cloud computing.
venue: IBM Journal of Research and Development

title: The Reservoir model and architecture for open federated cloud computing
abstract: Cloud computing promises scalable, on-demand IT services but faces significant limitations in scalability, interoperability, and business service management (BSM) support. This paper introduces the Reservoir model and architecture, designed to enable open federated cloud computing that addresses these deficiencies. The Reservoir approach proposes a modular, extensible architecture supporting dynamic federation among autonomous cloud providers, allowing seamless resource pooling and service provisioning across organizational boundaries while preserving provider autonomy. By embedding automated BSM and SLA management into the infrastructure, Reservoir facilitates reliable, cost-effective delivery of enterprise-grade services and democratizes cloud participation for small and medium-sized providers. The paper delineates motivations and use cases for federated clouds, defines a reference model and open architecture for interoperability, and presents a loosely coupled cloud stack with standardized interfaces. The Reservoir model establishes a foundation for next-generation cloud computing as a global utility, enabling competitive, flexible, and high-quality IT service delivery.

title: Universities in a competitive global marketplace
abstract: Purpose – The purpose of this systematic review was to explore the nature of the marketing of higher education (HE) and universities in an international context. The objectives of the review were to: systematically collect, document, scrutinise and critically analyse the current research literature on supply‐side higher education marketing; establish the scope of higher education marketing; identify gaps in the research literature; and make recommendations for further research in this field.Design/methodology/approach – The approach for this study entailed extensive searches of relevant business management and education databases. The intention was to ensure that, as far as possible, all literature in the field was identified – while keeping the focus on literature of greatest pertinence to the research questions.Findings – The paper finds that potential benefits of applying marketing theories and concepts that have been effective in the business world are gradually being recognised by researchers in the ...

title: Universities in a competitive global marketplace
abstract: This paper presents a systematic review of the literature on higher education marketing in the context of increasing global competition among universities. The review critically examines research on supply-side marketing strategies, focusing on the internationalisation and marketisation of higher education institutions. Findings indicate that while the adoption of business marketing concepts in higher education is growing, the field remains fragmented and lacks robust theoretical frameworks tailored to the unique characteristics of universities and their services. The literature reveals significant gaps, particularly regarding evidence of implemented marketing strategies by institutions, highlighting the need for further research from both exploratory and strategic perspectives. The paper concludes that higher education marketing is still at a pioneering stage, with substantial opportunities for future inquiry to address current limitations and inform institutional responses to global market dynamics.

title: What Is (Business) Management? Laying the Ground for a Philosophy of Management
abstract: In this article, we philosophically reflect on the nature of business management. We move beyond the political paradigm of the conceptualization of management in order to lay the ground for a philosophy of business management. First, we open-up the self-evident conceptualization of business management in contemporary management practices by comparing ancient and contemporary definitions of management. Second, we develop a framework with six dimensions of the nature of business management that can guide future philosophical and empirical work on the nature of business management: management control, people management, asset management and entrepreneurial action, management as participation, management as responsive action and management as constituting meaning.

title: What Is (Business) Management? Laying the Ground for a Philosophy of Management
abstract: This article critically examines the foundational question of what constitutes business management, moving beyond prevailing political and control-oriented paradigms to lay the groundwork for a philosophy of management. By juxtaposing ancient and contemporary definitions, the study challenges the self-evident conceptualization of management as mere managerial power or mechanism of control. Employing an explorative and confrontational philosophical method, the paper identifies limitations in traditional theories and introduces a framework comprising six dimensions—management control, people management, asset management and entrepreneurial action, participation, responsive action, and constituting meaning—that collectively capture the multifaceted nature of business management. This framework aims to open new avenues for philosophical and empirical inquiry, encouraging a more nuanced understanding of management that transcends reductionist models and addresses its broader organizational, social, and ethical implications.

title: 18F labeled nanoparticles for in vivo PET-CT imaging.
abstract: We report the synthesis and in vivo characterization of an 18F modified trimodal nanoparticle (18F-CLIO). This particle consists of cross-linked dextran held together in core-shell formation by a superparamagnetic iron oxide core and functionalized with the radionuclide 18F in high yield via 'click' chemistry. The particle can be detected with positron emission tomography, fluorescence molecular tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging. The presence of 18F dramatically lowers the detection threshold of the nanoparticles, while the facile conjugation chemistry provides a simple platform for rapid and efficient nanoparticle labeling.

title: 18F labeled nanoparticles for in vivo PET-CT imaging.
abstract: We describe the synthesis and in vivo evaluation of a novel 18F-labeled cross-linked dextran iron oxide nanoparticle (18F-CLIO) designed for trimodal imaging using positron emission tomography (PET), fluorescence molecular tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The 18F radiolabel was introduced via efficient copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (“click” chemistry) to an azide-modified nanoparticle, yielding high radiochemical purity and stability. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that 18F-CLIO enables highly sensitive PET detection at significantly lower concentrations than required for MRI, thereby reducing the necessary clinical dose. The straightforward labeling strategy leverages the widespread availability and favorable imaging properties of 18F, providing a robust platform for rapid nanoparticle functionalization and multimodal molecular imaging applications.

title: Advances in Bioconjugation.
abstract: Bioconjugation is a burgeoning field of research. Novel methods for the mild and site-specific derivatization of proteins, DNA, RNA, and carbohydrates have been developed for applications such as ligand discovery, disease diagnosis, and high-throughput screening. These powerful methods owe their existence to the discovery of chemoselective reactions that enable bioconjugation under physiological conditions-a tremendous achievement of modern organic chemistry. Here, we review recent advances in bioconjugation chemistry. Additionally, we discuss the stability of bioconjugation linkages-an important but often overlooked aspect of the field. We anticipate that this information will help investigators choose optimal linkages for their applications. Moreover, we hope that the noted limitations of existing bioconjugation methods will provide inspiration to modern organic chemists.

title: Advances in Bioconjugation.
abstract: Bioconjugation, the covalent modification of biomolecules, has emerged as a critical tool in chemical biology, enabling advances in ligand discovery, biochemical assays, diagnostics, imaging, and industrial catalysis. Recent progress in chemoselective reactions has facilitated the development of mild and site-specific bioconjugation methods applicable to proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates under physiological conditions. These innovations have expanded the utility of bioconjugates in high-throughput screening, biosensor design, and in vivo imaging, while also supporting the creation of more stable and functional biomolecule conjugates for therapeutic and industrial use. This review highlights key advances in bioconjugation chemistry, with particular emphasis on the stability of linkages—a crucial yet often underappreciated factor influencing bioconjugate performance. By summarizing current methodologies and their limitations, we aim to guide researchers in selecting optimal strategies for their applications and to inspire further innovation in the field.

title: Analytical chemistry of nitric oxide.
abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) is the focus of intense research primarily because of its wide-ranging biological and physiological actions. To understand its origin, activity, and regulation, accurate and precise measurement techniques are needed. Unfortunately, analytical assays for monitoring NO are challenged by NO's unique chemical and physical properties, including its reactivity, rapid diffusion, and short half-life. Moreover, NO concentrations may span the picomolar-to-micromolar range in physiological milieus, requiring techniques with wide dynamic response ranges. Despite such challenges, many analytical techniques have emerged for the detection of NO. Herein, we review the most common spectroscopic and electrochemical methods, with a focus on the underlying mechanism of each technique and on approaches that have been coupled with modern analytical measurement tools to create novel NO sensors.

title: Analytical chemistry of nitric oxide.
abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) is a critical signaling molecule with diverse physiological functions, necessitating accurate and sensitive analytical methods for its detection and quantification. The unique chemical and physical properties of NO—including high reactivity, rapid diffusion, and short half-life—pose significant challenges for measurement, especially given the wide concentration range encountered in biological systems. This review examines the most common spectroscopic and electrochemical techniques for NO analysis, emphasizing the underlying principles, analytical performance metrics, and strategies to enhance selectivity and sensitivity. Special attention is given to recent advances that integrate traditional assays with modern instrumentation or exploit novel sensor designs. Representative examples illustrate both established and emerging approaches for NO detection in complex matrices. The review highlights the importance of method selection based on application requirements and discusses prospects for future developments in NO analytical chemistry.

title: Anion receptor chemistry.
abstract: This article looks back at advances made in anion complexation since the turn of the millennium and ahead to the application of receptors in areas such as organocatalysis and nanotechnology.

title: Anion receptor chemistry.
abstract: This review summarizes key advances in anion receptor chemistry from 2013 to 2015, highlighting progress in the design and function of molecular systems capable of selective anion recognition and binding. The field has evolved from laboratory-based hydrogen-bonding receptors to more sophisticated systems employing diverse non-covalent interactions effective under real-world conditions. Notable developments include new receptor scaffolds such as arylboronic acids, squaramides, calixarenes, tetrazole-pyrrole-amides, polynorbornanes, and cyclopeptides, each offering unique binding modes and selectivities. These advances underpin applications in anion sensing, extraction, transport, catalysis, and self-assembly, with implications for environmental remediation, industrial separations, organocatalysis, and potential therapeutic strategies for diseases involving defective anion transport. The review emphasizes the interdisciplinary nature of anion receptor chemistry at the interface of supramolecular chemistry, materials science, and biology.

title: Aptamers from cell-based selection for bioanalytical applications.
abstract: Aptamers, single-stranded nucleic acids with high binding affinity and specificity, have emerged as powerful molecular recognition elements for bioanalytical applications. This review highlights the evolution of aptamer technology, focusing on cell-based selection methods (cell-SELEX) that enable the generation of aptamers targeting native cell surface proteins without prior knowledge of specific markers. Compared to traditional proteomic approaches, cell-SELEX offers significant advantages in biomarker discovery, detection, and profiling by capturing membrane proteins in their physiological context. The review discusses the principles of cell-SELEX, its methodological considerations, and its superiority over antibody-based techniques due to aptamers’ ease of synthesis, stability, low immunogenicity, and adaptability. Applications in cancer diagnostics and other biomedical fields are examined, illustrating how cell-SELEX-derived aptamers facilitate sensitive and specific detection of cellular targets. Challenges such as nonspecific interactions and optimization of selection conditions are addressed, with strategies to enhance selectivity and minimize background binding. Overall, cell-based aptamer selection represents a versatile platform for advancing bioanalytical technologies and personalized medicine through improved molecular recognition and biomarker identification.

abstract: This paper examines the Demand-Driven Acquisition (DDA) model for academic library ebook collections, highlighting its evolution, operational mechanisms, and benefits for both libraries and users. DDA enables libraries to provide immediate access to a vast selection of ebooks, with purchases or loans triggered only by meaningful user engagement, thereby optimizing budget efficiency and ensuring collections remain relevant to current academic needs. The model offers flexible options such as traditional DDA, Short-Term Loans, and Access-to-Own, allowing libraries to tailor acquisition strategies while maintaining control over selection and spending. Integration with platforms like Ebook Central, Rialto, and OASIS streamlines management and supports data-driven decision-making. Enhanced features—including customizable alerts, DRM-free downloads, scalable access models, and real-time usage analytics—further empower libraries to adapt to evolving research trends. User-centric collection development is reinforced through direct patron input, resulting in increased usage and satisfaction. The paper concludes that DDA represents a sustainable, adaptable approach to library collection development that aligns resource allocation with demonstrated user demand.

title: Asymmetric catalysis in organic synthesis
abstract: This research presents the development of novel asymmetric catalyst systems for enantioselective organic synthesis, focusing on lanthanide metals bearing diolate and Schiff-base ligands. The project aimed to address the growing demand for optically pure compounds in pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals by designing catalysts capable of transforming prochiral substrates into single enantiomer products with high efficiency and selectivity. Ligands were synthesized from inexpensive, readily available precursors using a modular approach, enabling rapid modification of ligand structures to optimize catalytic performance. The study also introduced a new ligand system for Group IV and lanthanide-based olefin polymerization catalysts, offering facile synthesis and tunable stereocontrol. The research demonstrated that these chiral lanthanide complexes exhibit significant Lewis acidity, facilitating strong substrate binding and effective enantioselective transformations. The findings highlight the potential of rational ligand design and structure-based catalyst optimization to advance asymmetric catalysis, providing scalable solutions for the production of enantiomerically pure compounds while minimizing waste and cost.

title: Atmospheric chemistry and global change
abstract: Atmospheric Chemistry and Global Change presents an integrated examination of chemical processes in the atmosphere, focusing on global-scale problems and their role in the evolution of the Earth system. Taking a largely interdisciplinary approach, it features the collective efforts of a group of scientists at the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR), as well as other experts from several universities and national laboratories. Ideal for graduate courses in atmospheric chemistry and atmospheric science, Atmospheric Chemistry and Global Change also serves as an authoritative and practical reference for scientists studying the Earth's atmosphere.

title: Atmospheric chemistry and global change
abstract: Atmospheric chemistry plays a central role in driving global environmental change by influencing climate, air quality, and the composition of the atmosphere. This paper reviews the complex interactions among chemical species in the atmosphere, examines the impact of human activities on atmospheric composition, and explores the consequences for climate change and ecosystem health. Key processes such as ozone depletion, greenhouse gas accumulation, and the formation of secondary pollutants are discussed in the context of both natural variability and anthropogenic forcing. The paper highlights advances in observational techniques and modeling that have improved our understanding of atmospheric processes, while emphasizing the need for continued research to predict future changes and inform policy decisions aimed at mitigating adverse impacts on the environment and society.

title: Attitudes toward chemistry among 11th grade students in high schools in Greece
abstract: The development of valid and reliable instruments for attitudes' measurement has been proven crucial for the quality of research. This study is dealing with the develop- ment and validation of an attitude toward chemistry instrument. By using this instrument, 11th grade Greek students' attitudes regarding the difficulty, the interest, the usefulness of chemistry course, and the importance of chemistry were investigated. Gender and study specialization differences in students' attitudes toward chemistry were examined for this population. Report card grades for the chemistry course were used to measure students' achievement in chemistry and its correlation with students' attitudes toward chemistry was explored. C

title: Attitudes toward chemistry among 11th grade students in high schools in Greece
abstract: This study examines the attitudes of 11th grade students in Greek high schools toward chemistry, focusing on perceived difficulty, interest, usefulness, and the importance of the subject. A new instrument was developed and validated to measure these attitudes, addressing common methodological challenges such as fakability, semantic issues, and dimensionality. The research also explores differences in attitudes based on gender and academic specialization, as well as the correlation between students’ chemistry achievement and their attitudes. Findings indicate that students generally perceive chemistry as difficult but recognize its usefulness and importance, with notable variations linked to gender and study track. The study highlights the need for discipline-specific attitude assessments and discusses implications for curriculum design and instructional practices in the Greek educational context.

title: A new local density functional for main-group thermochemistry, transition metal bonding, thermochemical kinetics, and noncovalent interactions.
abstract: We present a new local density functional, called M06-L, for main-group and transition element thermochemistry, thermochemical kinetics, and noncovalent interactions. The functional is designed to capture the main dependence of the exchange-correlation energy on local spin density, spin density gradient, and spin kinetic energy density, and it is parametrized to satisfy the uniform-electron-gas limit and to have good performance for both main-group chemistry and transition metal chemistry. The M06-L functional and 14 other functionals have been comparatively assessed against 22 energetic databases. Among the tested functionals, which include the popular B3LYP, BLYP, and BP86 functionals as well as our previous M05 functional, the M06-L functional gives the best overall performance for a combination of main-group thermochemistry, thermochemical kinetics, and organometallic, inorganometallic, biological, and noncovalent interactions. It also does very well for predicting geometries and vibrational frequencies. Because of the computational advantages of local functionals, the present functional should be very useful for many applications in chemistry, especially for simulations on moderate-sized and large systems and when long time scales must be addressed.

title: A new local density functional for main-group thermochemistry, transition metal bonding, thermochemical kinetics, and noncovalent interactions.
abstract: We introduce the M06-L local density functional, developed to address main-group and transition metal thermochemistry, thermochemical kinetics, and noncovalent interactions. M06-L incorporates dependence on local spin density, its gradient, and spin kinetic energy density, and is parameterized to satisfy the uniform electron gas limit while achieving balanced accuracy for both main-group and transition metal systems. Comprehensive benchmarking against 22 energetic databases demonstrates that M06-L outperforms 14 other functionals, including widely used hybrids such as B3LYP and previous functionals like M05, in predicting atomization energies, barrier heights, metal-ligand bonding, noncovalent interactions, molecular geometries, and vibrational frequencies. The computational efficiency of local functionals makes M06-L particularly advantageous for large or complex systems and long time-scale simulations, offering a practical and accurate tool for a broad range of chemical applications.

title: A Primer on Sediment-Trace Element Chemistry
abstract: This book provides a basic introduction to sediment-heavy metal interactions and how sediment chemical data can be used to address environmental questions and issues. It is designed to promote self-teaching and is written so that students and professionals with a minimum of formal training in the environmental sciences can understand it. The book addresses all of the major physical and chemical factors that control sediment-trace element chemistry, as well as sampling and sampling design, data manipulation, and data interpretation. Following in the steps of the successful first edition, which was used as a text for a three day short course for U.S. Geological Survey professionals interested in sediment trace chemistry and its application to water quality issues, A Primer on Sediment-Trace Element Chemistry, 2nd Edition is ideal for academics, geochemists, chemists, hydrologists, environmental lawyers, and water quality professionals needing a comprehensive introduction to this field.

title: A Primer on Sediment-Trace Element Chemistry
abstract: This primer provides a comprehensive overview of the principles and methodologies underlying sediment-trace element chemistry, emphasizing the critical role of sediments in the transport, partitioning, and historical record of trace elements in aquatic environments.
